content.text:
I have what I need. Here are your answers.

## 1. Where you'd start to create a new event (for testing)

There are two levels here, and the distinction matters for your testing goal:

**Create a whole new GROUP (recommended for isolated testing)**
- Go to **`/new`** → click the **"+" circle button** next to "Your groups" (labeled "Create new group")
- That's the page **`/new/create`** → fill in group name, optional logo, brand color → `POST /api/v2/orgs`
- You become `owner`, and it lands you at `/new/{slug}`
- This gives you a fully isolated tenant: its own members, events, financials, user statuses. Nothing you do here touches your real group.

**Create an EVENT inside an existing group**
- Go to **`/new/{slug}/admin`** → in the **Events** section, click the small **"+" button** ("New event")
- A modal collects: name, year, start/end date, location, and **status** (`draft` / `active` / `archived`) → `POST /api/v2/orgs/{id}/events`
- Note: only one event per group can be `active` at a time. Activating a new one auto-archives the current active event.

### Important for your use case
You said you want isolation specifically because you'll be "messing with user statuses." **v2 has no `test`/sandbox status** like the old v1 app did (`trip_settings.status='test'`). Events are only `draft`/`active`/`archived`. So the clean way to get a true sandbox is to **create a separate testing GROUP**, not just a test event inside your real group — because member records and user statuses live at the group level, not the event level. A test event inside your real group would still share the real member roster.

## 2. Where the master admin sees a list of all groups

**There isn't one today.** The `/new` landing page ("Your groups") only lists orgs *you're a member of* (`ctx.orgs`) — there's no platform-wide view. I confirmed there's no system-admin / superadmin concept wired up anywhere in the v2 code (no `is_system_admin`, no platform-admin gate). This matches your own planning note: the **system / group / group-feature admin tiers are still just planned (GH #178), not built.**

So right now, even as the person who owns the whole platform, you only see a group if you have a `v2_memberships` row in it. There's no God-view that enumerates every `v2_organizations` row through the UI.

That raises a natural question for how you want to proceed:

options.label: Test event in real group
options.description: Add a draft event inside your existing group. Shares the real member roster, so user-status changes would hit real members. Not truly isolated.

questions.question: Do you want me to build a master-admin 'all groups' view (GH #178 system-admin tier)?

options.label: Not now

options.label: Yes, plan it
options.description: Design the system-admin tier: a platform-wide groups list + a flag (e.g. v2_profiles.is_system_admin) gating it.

content.text:
I've got the full picture of the auth plumbing. Here's the plan for the system-admin "all groups" view. This is GH #178 (the admin-tiers note you already have), specifically the **system-admin tier**.

## Plan: System-admin "all groups" view

### The core problem
Today, `v2_organizations` RLS only exposes orgs you have a `v2_memberships` row in. `getPlatformContext()` builds "Your groups" purely from your memberships. So a master-admin view **cannot** go through the normal RLS client — it has to be a server-only route using the service-role (`v2AdminClient`) client, gated by an explicit flag.

### 1. Schema — new migration `00251_v2_system_admin.sql`
Add the flag to `v2_profiles`:
```sql
ALTER TABLE public.v2_profiles
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_system_admin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
```
No new grant needed (column on an already-granted table). RLS stays self-only — the flag is **never** read through the cookie client, only the service-role client, so a user can't escalate themselves.

**Bootstrap decision:** nothing grants this flag yet, so the migration must seed the first sysadmin (you). Since v2 is phone/SMS-auth, I'd match on your `auth.users` phone or email:
```sql
UPDATE public.v2_profiles SET is_system_admin = true
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM auth.users WHERE email = 'claude.ai@jeffblankenburg.com' OR phone = '<your-phone>');
```

### 2. Server helper — `src/lib/v2/orgs.ts`
Mirror the existing `isAnyOrgAdmin` pattern:
```ts
export async function isSystemAdmin(admin: SupabaseClient, userId: string): Promise<boolean>
```
Reads `v2_profiles.is_system_admin` via the service-role client.

### 3. Context — `src/lib/v2/context.ts`
Add `isSystemAdmin: boolean` to `PlatformContext` (computed once with the admin client), so server components can branch without extra round-trips.

### 4. The view — `/new/admin` (platform-level, NOT org-scoped)
New route `src/app/new/admin/page.tsx`. Server component: if `!ctx?.isSystemAdmin` → `redirect("/new")`. Lists **all** orgs from `v2_organizations` (service-role client) with: name/logo, slug, member count, event count, created date, owner name. Each row links to `/new/{slug}`. Respects the 1000-row cap note — order by `created_at desc`, paginate if it ever grows (fine for now).

### 5. Entry point — `/new/page.tsx`
When `ctx.isSystemAdmin`, show an "All groups (admin)" link near the "Your groups" title, routing to `/new/admin`. Invisible to everyone else.

### 6. (Optional, later) grant/revoke UI
For now the flag is migration-seeded. A UI to promote other sysadmins can come later — out of scope for this first cut.

---

Two things I want your call on before I build:

Both noted. One thing I need from you, then I'll build the whole thing (View + manage).

**What's the phone number tied to your v2 SMS-OTP login?** I'll match on `auth.users.phone` in the bootstrap `UPDATE`. v2 stores phones in E.164 (e.g. `+16145551234`), so give it to me however you like and I'll normalize.

While you grab that, here's exactly what **View + manage** will include so there are no surprises:

**View** (`/new/admin`, sysadmin-gated)
- All groups: logo, name, slug, member count, event count, created date, owner
- Each row deep-links into `/new/{slug}`

**Manage**
- **Promote/demote system admins** — a section listing current sysadmins with add (by member) / remove, writing `v2_profiles.is_system_admin`. Guardrail: you can't demote the last remaining sysadmin (lockout prevention), same spirit as not deleting the last owner.
- **Per-org quick actions** — "Open" (jump into the group) and "Impersonate owner" via the existing v2 simulator (`resolveEffectiveUser`), so you can walk a group's admin experience for support/testing. 

I'll leave **destructive** per-org actions (delete/archive a whole group) out of this first cut unless you want them — deleting a tenant cascades across every `v2_` table and deserves its own careful pass.

Give me the phone number and I'll start.
Phone noted — I'll normalize `6143275066` to `+16143275066`. Now let me read the patterns I need to match (simulator, API guard, admin client, styling) before writing anything.

-- 00251_v2_system_admin.sql
-- Platform "system admin" tier (GH #178). A system admin is a PLATFORM-level
-- operator who can see and manage every group (v2_organizations), independent of
-- per-org membership/role. The flag lives on v2_profiles and is NEVER read through
-- the RLS cookie client — only the service-role client reads it server-side — so a
-- user can't escalate themselves by writing their own profile row.

ALTER TABLE public.v2_profiles
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_system_admin BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false;

-- Bootstrap the first system admin (Jeff). Nothing in the app grants this flag yet,
-- so seed it here. Match on the SMS-OTP phone (digits-normalized against both the
-- 11-digit country-coded and 10-digit forms) with an email fallback.
UPDATE public.v2_profiles p
SET is_system_admin = true
FROM auth.users u
WHERE p.id = u.id
  AND (
    regexp_replace(COALESCE(u.phone, ''), '\D', '', 'g') IN ('16143275066', '6143275066')
    OR u.email = 'claude.ai@jeffblankenburg.com'
  );

-- Cross-org overview for the system-admin "all groups" screen. Does the per-org
-- member/event COUNTs in SQL (one row per org) so the app never has to pull every
-- membership row client-side and trip the 1000-row select cap. Read ONLY via the
-- service-role client (RLS on v2_organizations would otherwise hide other orgs).
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS public.v2_org_overview;
CREATE VIEW public.v2_org_overview AS
SELECT
  o.id,
  o.name,
  o.slug,
  o.logo_url,
  o.primary_color,
  o.created_at,
  o.created_by,
  (SELECT p.display_name FROM public.v2_profiles p WHERE p.id = o.created_by) AS creator_name,
  (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM public.v2_memberships m
    WHERE m.org_id = o.id AND m.status = 'active' AND m.archived_at IS NULL
  ) AS member_count,
  (
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM public.v2_events e WHERE e.org_id = o.id
  ) AS event_count,
  (
    SELECT e.name FROM public.v2_events e
    WHERE e.org_id = o.id AND e.status = 'active'
    ORDER BY e.created_at DESC LIMIT 1
  ) AS active_event_name
FROM public.v2_organizations o;

-- Server-only. Keep the overview out of reach of the anon/authenticated RLS clients.
GRANT SELECT ON public.v2_org_overview TO service_role;

Everything typechecks and lints clean, and I've recorded the shipped tier in memory. Here's what I built and how to verify it.

## What I built: system-admin "all groups" console (GH #178, tier 1)

**Foundation**
- **`00251_v2_system_admin.sql`** — adds `v2_profiles.is_system_admin` (default false), **bootstraps your flag** by matching `+16143275066` (digit-normalized, with an email fallback), and creates a service-role-only `v2_org_overview` view that does per-org member/event counts *in SQL* so the list never trips the 1000-row select cap.
- **`isSystemAdmin()`** helper in `src/lib/v2/orgs.ts`, surfaced on `PlatformContext.isSystemAdmin` in `context.ts`.
- Extended **`canSimulate`** so a system admin can impersonate *anyone*, including owners of groups they don't belong to (the normal gate requires a shared org).

**The console — `/new/admin`** (server page + `PlatformAdmin.tsx` client, gated: non-sysadmins redirect to `/new`)
- **All groups**: every org with logo, member/event counts, active event, created date/creator, plus **Open** and **View as {owner}** (impersonate via the existing simulator).
- **System admins**: current roster with **Remove**, and a member search to **Add** — both confirmed via `ConfirmModal`, with a **last-admin lockout guard** on client *and* server (`/api/v2/admin/system-admins`, which gates on the *real* caller, not the simulated one).

**Entry points**
- `/new` chooser shows a "Platform admin, all groups" link (and no longer auto-redirects single-org sysadmins past it).
- A "Platform" tile in each group's admin hub.

1. **Run the migration** (it hasn't been applied — do this first) against your Supabase DB.
2. **Confirm the bootstrap matched you** — this is the one thing that can lock you out. Run:

   ```sql
   SELECT p.id, p.display_name, p.is_system_admin, u.phone
   FROM v2_profiles p JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = p.id
   WHERE p.is_system_admin;
   ```

   If that returns **no rows**, the phone format in `auth.users` differs — fix with:
   ```sql
   UPDATE v2_profiles SET is_system_admin = true
   WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM auth.users WHERE phone LIKE '%6143275066%');
   ```

3. **Happy path** — load `/new`, click "Platform admin, all groups" → see every group with correct counts. Click **Open** on your test group.

Clean. Here's the fix and why it was needed.

## What was wrong
Your orange *was* being saved to the database — the gap was on the display side. The theme color (`--brand`) was only ever applied in two places:
- The **root** `/new/layout.tsx`, but only for **custom domains** (it resolves the org by hostname, which returns nothing for a path like `/new/tko-trivia`).
- The hardcoded default green in `new.module.css`.

The `/new/[slug]` layout *had* your org (color and all) in context but never pushed `primary_color` into the CSS cascade, so every path-based group fell back to green.

## The fix
`src/app/new/[slug]/layout.tsx` now wraps the whole group subtree in a `display: contents` element that sets `--brand` from `org.primary_color`. That carries your orange down to everything using `--brand` (monograms, buttons, section labels, event title, active states, nav accents) with zero layout impact, and falls back to the default green if a group has no color set.

## Verify
1. Reload `/new/tko-trivia` → accents (buttons, monogram, section labels, the event title) should now be orange.
2. Change the color in **Admin → Settings** and reload → the new color applies site-wide for that group.

So on the original site, saying "attending" auto-added you to the day's contests. That cascade **hasn't been ported to v2 yet** — contest enrollment is currently a manual step you do on the contest's **Teams** page. "Round 1" is a scramble with nobody enrolled, hence 0 players / 0 teams.

I dug into both the current v2 state and the v1 precedent for all three. Your instincts are right — and the good news is this isn't greenfield: **v1 already solved most of this**, and v2 already has the one piece v1 lacked. Here's what grounds the plan.

## What I found

**The cascade already exists in v1.** `src/lib/attendance-contest-sync.ts` is a mature engine: when someone becomes "Attending," it auto-enrolls them into the blanket contests (`auto_enroll_attendees` = scramble/calcutta/ryder); when they leave, it does a **guarded** removal that refuses to orphan a scramble seat / Calcutta bid / Ryder pairing and returns **warnings**. There's even an opt-out tombstone (`contest_enrollment_exclusions`) so re-RSVPing doesn't re-add someone who deliberately left a contest.

**v2 has none of that yet** — `v2_contest_participants` is a bare join table, the participants API is read-only, RSVP explicitly notes "enrollment sync lands when v2 contests do," and there are zero removal guards.

**But here's the kicker for your #3:** v1 computes those warnings and then *throws them away* — the admin grid silently discards them. So v1's biggest weakness is exactly the thing you're asking for. v2 can do it properly because it already has a **full notification system** (`v2_notifications` + `sendV2Notifications` + web push + per-user prefs) that v1's attendance flow never used. We can target org admins directly and push "someone just bailed off a team" to their phone.

**On money:** buy-ins live in `v2_cost_items` keyed to the contest (single source, #213). There is **no per-member balance anywhere** — no ledger, no "owes," no paid flag per participant. The Financials screen is catalog-level only (totals per contest), and nothing member-facing exists. So "it should appear in their balance owed" means building the member dimension that doesn't exist yet.

## The design — one subsystem, three issues

I'd treat these as one lifecycle (**attendance → enrollment → money → integrity**) shipped in three dependent pieces:

**A. Enrollment (your #1).** Add `v2_contests.auto_enroll_attendees` (defaulted by type, like v1). On contest *create*, enroll everyone currently on-roster. Add the missing participants write API (POST/DELETE) and an **"Import attendees"** action on the contest page — "add all" or pick a subset — honoring a v2 opt-out tombstone so removals stick.

**B. Money (your #2).** A member's balance = sum of buy-ins for contests they're in (derived), plus a **paid flag** (the one thing you can't derive). Surface it two ways: an admin per-member "who owes / who's paid / reconcile" view in Financials, and a member-facing "what you owe."

**C. Integrity + alerts (your #3).** Port v1's guarded sync to v2, but *finish the job v1 didn't*: when an attendance change removes someone who's on a team (or later, a tee time), fire a `contest_roster_break` notification to all org admins (in-app + push, deep-linked to the Teams page) and mark the team "needs attention." Build C on top of A.

content.text:
Here's exactly how v1 does it — and it answers the money-model question by precedent.

## v1 is a unified transaction ledger (not a paid-flag model)

The core is one table, **`financial_transactions`** — an append-only log, one row per money event:

```
financial_transactions
  user_id, trip_id
  type     'charge' | 'payment'
  source   option | contest_entry | manual | adjustment |
           deposit | withdrawal | winnings | credit | expense
  amount   numeric(10,2)  (always > 0; direction comes from `type`)
  description, method, notes
  option_id, financial_contest_id    (what the row is tied to)
  created_by, created_at
```

**Net balance is derived, never stored:** `balance = SUM(payments) − SUM(charges)`, computed at read time (`/api/financials/me:70-87`). Negative = they owe; positive = they're owed/have credit.

How money enters the ledger:
- **Charges (member → pot):** selecting a trip option inserts a `source='option'` charge; being added to a paid contest inserts a `source='contest_entry'` charge (`admin/financials/contest-participants:114-136` — `entry_fee × quantity`); admins can add `manual`/`adjustment`/`expense` charges.
- **Payments (pot → member or cash in):** `deposit` (they paid Venmo/cash), `winnings`, `credit`, `adjustment`.

A few **special per-item paid flags** sit *alongside* the ledger for things that need explicit state: `pickem_payments.paid` and `contest_winners.paid` (payout side). But the general "what you owe" is pure ledger math.

What members/admins see:
- **Member** (`MyFinancials.tsx`): one big net-balance number + a searchable transaction list, and a "Pay Sheiker $X" Venmo button when negative.
- **Admin** (`FinancialGrid.tsx`): grid of everyone — charges / payments / net — scoped to this trip or lifetime, with drill-down into each person's full ledger. Edits are audited in `financial_transaction_history`.

## What this means for your three challenges

The ledger model is the right answer, and it's the thing you set as a principle ("v2 mirrors the original"). Notably, it already handles the nuances I flagged earlier:

- **Partial payments / credits / refunds** — v1 has no state machine for them, but the ledger gets them *for free*: a $20 payment against $40 of charges just nets to −$20. Credits and adjustments are ordinary rows.
- **Your #2 falls out naturally** — enrolling someone in a paid contest = insert a `contest_entry` charge row → it shows in their balance immediately. Un-enrolling = reverse it (delete the row, or post an offsetting adjustment).
- **Re-pricing** — v1 even re-derives option costs from `cost_items` at read time, so balances track current prices.

So my recommendation flips from what I offered before: **mirror v1's ledger** (`v2_financial_transactions` + derived net balance + read-time cost_items pricing), rather than the minimal paid-flag. It's more table, but it's the proven model, it's consistent with the rest of v2, and it makes #2 trivial.

One caveat worth naming: v2's buy-ins currently live only in `v2_cost_items` as a *catalog* (amount per contest, not per person). The ledger adds the **per-person** dimension v2 doesn't have yet — the two coexist (catalog = "what this contest costs"; ledger = "what Jeff owes because he's in it").

Want me to lock in "mirror the v1 ledger" as the money model? If so, the two decisions still genuinely open are: **(a)** what a regular member sees (full line items like v1, or just a net number per your #125 trip-cost rule), and **(b)** the bail behavior when teams/tee-times exist (I can mirror v1's split: member-initiated RSVP = hard cascade, admin toggle = guarded with warnings — now surfaced via notifications, which v1 never did).

Items that are not part of "Trip Cost" will be grouped into "Options" eventually.  We haven't built that for v2.  Generally, you can't pick "part" of an option.  You are in for all of it, or none of it.  For example, the Closest to the Pin "option" will include all of the CTP contests from all of the days.  So users will see one item, "Closest to the Pin" that costs $15, even though it is technically 6 x $2.50.

That example locks the model into focus. The Option is the member-facing unit, and v1's wiring matches your description exactly: a "Closest to the Pin" option links (through `cost_items`) to the 6 daily CTP contests, its price is the **sum** of those cost_items (6 × $2.50 = $15), and selecting it writes **one** `source='option'` charge for $15 while enrolling you into all 6 `contest_participants` rows. Deselect = all 6 come off. All-or-nothing, one line, one price. v2 has the `cost_items` substrate but none of the Option grouping, selections, or ledger on top of it.

So the whole thing resolves into **two enrollment lanes**, and your three challenges split cleanly across them:

## Lane A — "Included" (blanket, part of attending)
Scramble, Calcutta, Ryder. Auto-enroll when `on_roster`. **No charge** (folded into Trip Cost). This is where:
- **Your #1** lives — "import attendees into a new contest" = the auto-enroll cascade (enroll everyone currently attending when the contest is created, plus a manual add/remove for stragglers, with an opt-out tombstone).
- **Your #3** lives — someone bails, and because they were on a team/tee time, the guarded-removal + **admin notification** kicks in.

## Lane B — "Options" (opt-in, paid bundles)
CTP, Skins, Cornhole, Pickem, etc. The member picks the **whole Option**; it bundles 1..N contests; one price; **one ledger charge**; enroll-into-all / deselect-removes-all. This is where:
- **Your #2** lives — adding/selecting a paid Option posts a `contest_entry`/`option` charge to the ledger → it appears in their balance instantly; reversing it removes the charge.

The **ledger** (`v2_financial_transactions`, mirroring v1) underpins both, and net balance stays derived (`payments − charges`).

## What this settles

- **Money model** → mirror v1's ledger. Your "can't pick part of an option / one $15 line" requirement is exactly why — the ledger charges at the *Option* level, not per-contest. Decision made by precedent.
- **Member visibility** → members see **Trip Cost + a list of Options**, each a single name + price (never the 6 CTP contests inside). That's fully consistent with your #125 rule (members never see the line items behind a bundle). So that question answers itself too.
- The **Options layer is a prerequisite** for #2 — it's the "options + payouts next" phase already on the v2 financials roadmap. #2 can't really ship without it.

## What's still genuinely open

Only the **bail behavior** (Lane A). My recommendation is to mirror v1's *split*, but finish the job v1 didn't:
- **Member drops their own RSVP** → honor reality, hard-cascade them off teams/contests (they're not coming) — but fire the admin notification v1 never sent.
- **Admin toggles someone off** → guarded removal: refuse to silently orphan a team seat, surface a warning, and notify.

Either way the new capability is the **immediate admin alert** (in-app + push, deep-linked to the affected team), which v2 can do and v1 structurally couldn't.

Does that two-lane shape match how you think about it? If so, the natural build/issue order is: **(1)** the ledger + Lane-A auto-enroll/import, **(2)** the Options layer + Lane-B charges + balances UI, **(3)** the bail-integrity + admin notifications on top of #1. I can write these up as GitHub issues (epic + three) with this model baked in — want me to draft them?
Yes. We can think of "Trip Cost" as one big option.

Yes — and that unifies it beautifully: **Trip Cost is just the one auto-derived, always-included Option** whose price is the sum of its `included_in_trip_cost` cost_items. So the member's whole financial view becomes "a list of Options," Trip Cost being the first (mandatory, derived) one, mirroring v1's `option_type='trip_cost'` exactly.

# v2: enrollment, member balances & attendance integrity (epic)

The lifecycle that ties attendance, contests, and money together in v2. Today these are disconnected: marking a member "Attending" (`v2_event_participants`) does nothing to contest enrollment (`v2_contest_participants`), contest buy-ins live only as a catalog (`v2_cost_items`) with **no per-member balance**, and nothing reacts when an attending member bails. v1 solved all of this; v2 has ported none of it. This epic ports the model — and fixes the one place v1 fell short (it computed roster-break warnings and then threw them away).

Builds on **#213** (cost_items money spine + financials screen) and **#209** (contests-as-spine / side games). This is #213's phases 3–4 plus the per-member dimension #213 never built.

## The core mental model: two enrollment lanes

Every contest reaches a member through exactly one of two lanes:

**Lane A — "Included" (blanket, part of attending).** Scramble, Calcutta, Ryder. Auto-enrolled when the member is `on_roster`. **No separate charge** — folded into Trip Cost. The member doesn't opt in; attending *is* opting in.

**Lane B — "Options" (opt-in, paid bundles).** CTP, Skins, Cornhole, Pickem, etc. The member picks a whole **Option**, which is **all-or-nothing** and may bundle *many* contests. Example: the "Closest to the Pin" Option costs **$15** and enrolls you in all **6** daily CTP contests (6 × $2.50). The member sees one line, one price — never the six contests inside.

**Trip Cost is just one special Option** — auto-derived, always-included, price = `SUM(cost_items WHERE included_in_trip_cost)`. So the member's entire financial view is "a list of Options," Trip Cost being the first (mandatory, derived) one.

The **ledger** (`v2_financial_transactions`, mirroring v1) records per-member charges/payments; net balance stays derived (`payments − charges`). Catalog (`v2_cost_items`) = "what things cost"; ledger = "what *this member* owes."

## Sub-issues

1. **Attendance ↔ contest enrollment sync (Lane A)** — auto-enroll on attend, import attendees into a newly added contest (all/subset), opt-out tombstone, participants write API. (your challenge #1)
2. **Options layer + per-member ledger + balances (Lane B + money)** — `v2_options` + selections + `v2_financial_transactions`; Option select → one charge + enroll into bundled contests; member-facing balance + admin per-member reconcile. (your challenge #2)
3. **Attendance-change integrity + admin alerts (Lane A integrity)** — guarded removal, member-RSVP hard-cascade vs admin-toggle guarded, and the new immediate **admin notification** (in-app + push) when a status change orphans a team seat / tee time. Depends on #1. (your challenge #3)

## Build order
1 → 2 → 3. (3 needs 1's sync engine; 2 is independent of 3 and can overlap with 1.)

## v1 precedent to mirror
- `src/lib/attendance-contest-sync.ts` — the blanket auto-enroll + guarded removal engine.
- `src/lib/option-contest-sync.ts` — Option select/deselect → enroll/remove across all bundled contests.
- `financial_transactions` (ledger) + `src/app/api/financials/me/route.ts` — derived net balance.
- `trip_options` (incl. `option_type='trip_cost'`), `cost_items.linked_option_id`, `cost_item_option_choices` — the Option→cost→contest wiring.
- `contests.auto_enroll_attendees`, `contest_enrollment_exclusions` — the blanket flag + opt-out tombstone.

## Parity note
v1 surfaced guarded-removal warnings in the API response but the admin UI silently discarded them (`AttendanceGrid.tsx`). v2's win: a real notification system (`v2_notifications` + `sendV2Notifications` + web push) lets us alert admins immediately. Sub-issue 3 is explicitly the fix for that gap.

# v2: attendance ↔ contest enrollment sync + import attendees (Lane A)

Part of #214. Ports v1's blanket auto-enroll so "Attending" actually populates the contests a member is in, and gives admins a way to pull current attendees into a contest added *after* people RSVP'd.

Today in v2: `v2_contest_participants` is a bare join table, the participants API is read-only, RSVP (`/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`) explicitly notes "enrollment sync lands when v2 contests do," and there is no auto-enroll. So a contest shows **0 players** even when 41 members are attending — exactly the confusion that kicked this off.

## Scope

**Lane A only** (blanket/included contests: scramble, calcutta, ryder). Opt-in Options (CTP/skins/etc.) are sub-issue 2. No money here — Lane A contests are folded into Trip Cost.

## Model

- **`v2_contests.auto_enroll_attendees BOOLEAN DEFAULT false`** — mirrors v1 00165. Defaulted `true` at create time for blanket contest types (scramble / calcutta / ryder), `false` for opt-in types. Admin can toggle.
- **`v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions`** (new table, mirrors v1) — tombstone of "this member explicitly left this contest; don't auto-re-add." `(contest_id, user_id)` unique, `removed_by`, `reason`, `removed_at`. Distinct from a full roster leave.
- Enrollment stays `v2_contest_participants (contest_id, user_id)`.

## Behavior

1. **On attend** (`on_roster` → true, from RSVP 99 or admin toggle): additively upsert the member into every `auto_enroll_attendees=true` contest in the event, **except** contests they have an exclusion tombstone for. Idempotent.
2. **On contest create** with `auto_enroll_attendees=true`: enroll everyone currently `on_roster` (minus tombstones). This is the "admin adds a contest after people enrolled" case.
3. **Manual import UI** on the contest page: "Import attendees" → **add all** on-roster members, or pick a **subset**. Picking a subset that omits someone, or removing an auto-enrolled member, writes an exclusion tombstone so the next attend-sync doesn't silently re-add them.
4. **Manual add/remove** of individual participants (admin), writing tombstones on removal.

(Removal driven by an *attendance drop* — and its team/tee-time guards + admin alerts — is sub-issue 3. This issue is the additive + manual-admin side.)

## API

- `POST /api/v2/orgs/[id]/events/[eventId]/contests/[contestId]/participants` — add one/many (body `{ userIds: [] }` or `{ importAll: true }`); clears tombstones for added users.
- `DELETE …/participants` — remove one/many; writes exclusion tombstones (`removed_by`, optional `reason`).
- Extend the existing contest-create path to run auto-enroll when the flag is set.
- Shared helper `syncAttendanceEnrollment(admin, eventId, userId, onRoster)` in `src/lib/v2/contests/` — called from the RSVP route and admin attendance writes (additive path now; guarded-removal path lands in #3).

## UX

- Contest page "Teams/Players" area: a players list + **Import attendees** button → modal (select all / search + check subset). Show the auto-enroll toggle in contest settings with a one-line explainer ("Everyone attending is automatically in this contest").
- Reuse existing member-row + modal patterns; v2 design system.

## Edge cases
- Re-running import is idempotent (upsert).
- A member with a tombstone is skipped by import-all and by attend-sync until re-added explicitly (which clears the tombstone).
- Guests / non-members: not applicable (contest participants are profiles).
- Respect the 1000-row cap on any attendee/member fetch.

## Acceptance criteria
- Marking a member Attending enrolls them into all blanket contests (minus tombstones).
- Creating a blanket contest after RSVPs enrolls current attendees.
- "Import attendees" adds all or a chosen subset; the contest player count reflects it immediately.
- Removing a participant prevents auto-re-add (tombstone) until explicitly re-added.
- No money side effects (that's #2).

## v1 reference
`src/lib/attendance-contest-sync.ts`, migration `00165_attendance_contest_autoenroll.sql`, `src/app/api/admin/contests/route.ts` (AUTO_ENROLL_TYPES).

# v2: Options layer + per-member ledger + balances (Lane B + money)

Part of #214. Realizes #213's phases 3–4 **and** adds the per-member dimension #213's catalog model never had. This is where "adding a member to a paid contest shows up in their balance owed" actually happens.

Today in v2: buy-ins live in `v2_cost_items` as a catalog (amount per contest/side-game), the financials screen is aggregate-only, and there is **no concept of what a specific member owes** — no ledger, no paid state, nothing member-facing.

## Two new layers

### 1. Options (`v2_options` + selections) — the member-facing unit
An **Option** is an all-or-nothing, opt-in purchase that may bundle **many** contests. "Closest to the Pin" = one $15 line that enrolls you in all 6 daily CTP contests. Members never see the inner contests — one name, one price (consistent with the #125 rule: members see bundles, not line items).

- **`v2_options`**: `id, org_id, event_id, name, description, option_type (checkbox|select|multi_select|quantity), choices JSONB, sort_order, icon`. Price is **derived** from linked cost_items, never stored (matches v1 + #213 §32).
- **Trip Cost is the one derived, always-included Option**: price = `SUM(cost_items WHERE included_in_trip_cost)`. Not a row members toggle — the mandatory first line.
- **Option → contests** via the cost_items the option links (`v2_cost_items.linked_option_id`, and `v2_cost_item_option_choices` for per-choice bundles). A contest's buy-in is a cost_item; an Option groups those cost_items; selecting the Option enrolls into every contest whose buy-in cost_item the Option funds.
- **`v2_user_option_selections`** `(event_id, user_id, option_id, value JSONB)`, unique `(user_id, option_id)`.
- **`syncOptionContestEnrollment`** (port of v1 `option-contest-sync.ts`): select → upsert the member into **all** bundled contests' `v2_contest_participants`; deselect → remove from all. All-or-nothing, idempotent.

### 2. Ledger (`v2_financial_transactions`) — what each member owes
Port of v1's `financial_transactions`. Append-only; net balance derived (`SUM(payment) − SUM(charge)`).

```
v2_financial_transactions
  id, org_id, event_id
  user_id        NOT NULL → v2_profiles
  type           'charge' | 'payment'
  source         'option' | 'contest_entry' | 'manual' | 'adjustment' | 'deposit' | 'winnings' | 'credit' | 'expense'
  amount_cents   INTEGER NOT NULL (>0; direction from `type`)
  option_id      → v2_options (set when source='option')
  description, method, notes
  created_by, created_at
```

- Selecting an Option writes **one** `source='option'` charge for the Option's total (e.g. $15), **not** one per bundled contest — and enrolls into all contests (layer 1). Deselect reverses the charge + enrollment.
- Re-pricing at read time from cost_items (v1 behavior) so balances track current prices.
- Member balance is **lifetime-or-per-event** TBD in build — default per-event, matching how v1 shows a trip balance.

## UX

- **Member-facing "What you owe"**: Trip Cost (single number) + a list of Options (each a name + price + select toggle) + net balance + paid/unpaid. Never the contest breakdown behind a bundle.
- **RSVP / event page**: Options selection lives alongside attendance (selecting a paid Option is the opt-in).
- **Admin financials** (extend #213 screen): a **per-member balances tab** — everyone's charges / payments / net, scope to event attendees, drill into one member's ledger, **record a payment** / adjustment / credit (reconcile). Mirrors v1 `FinancialGrid` + ledger modal.

## Open product decision (confirm in build)
Member visibility defaults to **Options-as-single-lines** (name + price, no inner contests) per #125. If a member should instead see only a single net number with no per-option breakdown, that's a smaller variant — decide before the member view ships.

## Edge cases
- Option with zero-cost choices → no charge row.
- Changing a selection deletes the old `source='option'` charge for that option and writes the new one (no soft-delete), and re-syncs enrollment diffs.
- An attendance drop that removes a member from a *paid* option's contests must also reverse the charge — coordinate with #3.
- `included_in_trip_cost` AND `linked_option_id` on the same cost_item is invalid (reconcile to one bucket) — enforce (per #213 §30).
- Partial payments / credits fall out of the ledger for free (a $10 payment against $15 nets to −$5).

## Acceptance criteria
- Selecting the CTP Option writes one $15 charge and enrolls the member in all 6 CTP contests; deselecting reverses both.
- A member's balance = Trip Cost + selected Options − payments, shown member-facing as single lines.
- Admin can see every member's net, drill into a ledger, and record payments/adjustments.
- Trip Cost renders as the derived, always-included Option.

## v1 reference
`trip_options` (+ `option_type='trip_cost'`), `src/lib/option-contest-sync.ts`, `src/app/api/selections/route.ts`, `financial_transactions`, `src/app/api/financials/me/route.ts`, `src/components/admin/FinancialGrid.tsx`, `src/lib/cost-items/compute.ts` (read-time pricing).

# v2: attendance-change integrity + immediate admin alerts (Lane A integrity)

Part of #214. Depends on #<ENROLL>. The hard one: a member who was "Attending" when teams/tee times were built later bails, and that quietly breaks a scramble team (empty seat), a tee time, or a Calcutta lot. An admin must **know immediately**.

This is the fix for v1's single biggest weakness here: v1 *computed* guarded-removal warnings and then threw them away — the admin grid (`AttendanceGrid.tsx`) silently discarded them. v2 has a real notification system, so we finish the job.

## What breaks when a participant leaves (v2 today: nothing guards it)
- `v2_scramble_team_members` — an orphaned/empty team seat (no FK cascade, no guard).
- `v2_scramble_hole_scores` — scores tied to a now-broken team.
- `v2_contest_winners` — if they'd already been recorded a winner.
- Tee times — v2 has only a `v2_scramble_teams.tee_time` field today (no pairing table yet); guard the seat, extend when real tee times land.
- Paid Options (#<OPTIONS>) — leaving a paid contest must reverse the ledger charge.

## Behavior (mirror v1's split, then alert)

**Member drops their own RSVP** (likelihood < 99 via `/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`): honor reality — they're not coming. Hard-cascade them off teams, blanket contests, and paid options (reversing those charges). This matches v1's `cascadeRemoveFromRoster`. **New:** fire an admin alert for every contest where the removal left a hole (empty team seat, etc.).

**Admin toggles someone off** (admin attendance write): **guarded** removal — refuse to silently orphan protected state (on a scramble team, has a tee time, is a recorded winner, has a Calcutta bid when that lands). Remove from unprotected contests, return warnings for the protected ones, and alert so the admin can unwind by hand. Matches v1's `protectedContests`.

In both paths the member leaves the event roster; the difference is how aggressively protected contest state is torn down vs. preserved-with-warning.

## The alert (the actual new capability)
- New notification type `contest_roster_break` in the v2 notification catalog (`notification-prefs.ts`).
- On a roster-affecting removal, send via `sendV2Notifications` to **all active org owners/admins** (query `v2_memberships` `role IN ('owner','admin')`, `status='active'`, `archived_at IS NULL`). In-app row **and** web push.
- Deep-link `data.url` to the affected contest's Teams page.
- Title/body name the member + what broke ("Dana Reyes left — Team 3 now has an empty seat in Round 1").

## "Needs attention" surfacing (in-app, beyond the push)
- Flag the affected team/contest as **needs attention** (derived: a team with fewer members than expected, or an enrolled seat whose member is no longer `on_roster`). Badge it on the contest list + Teams page so it's visible even if the push is missed.
- No new table needed if derivable; add a lightweight `needs_attention_at` only if derivation is too expensive.

## Edge cases
- Member re-RSVPs "Attending" after bailing: additive re-enroll (per #<ENROLL>), but do **not** silently reinstate a torn-down team seat — leave that to the admin (surface it as resolved/needs-review).
- Simulator-suppressed notifications inherited from `sendV2Notifications`.
- Best-effort alerts: a notification failure never blocks the attendance write.
- Don't double-alert on a no-op (member already off).

## Acceptance criteria
- A member dropping RSVP while on a team removes them and fires an admin push + in-app alert deep-linking to that team.
- Admin toggling off a member on a team gets a warning + alert and the protected seat isn't silently orphaned.
- Leaving a paid option reverses the member's ledger charge (coord. #<OPTIONS>).
- The affected contest/team shows a "needs attention" badge until an admin resolves it.
- No alert on no-op removals.

## v1 reference

Corrected everywhere (#214/#215/#216 + memory). The model is now simpler and keyed entirely off the flag you already have:

- **The lane = `cost_items.included_in_trip_cost`.** No new `auto_enroll_attendees` flag — that was me over-engineering. The admin already sets the lane by reconciling a contest's buy-in cost_item to **Trip Cost** vs **an Option** on the existing #213 Financials screen.
- **Included** (`included_in_trip_cost = true`) = part of the base price everyone attending pays → auto-enrolled, no separate charge. Can even be a $0 cost_item (a free-but-mandatory contest). This is #215's territory, and "import attendees" applies only here.
- **Optional** (anything not in Trip Cost) = **must have an Option created to represent it** to the member. Opt-in, and **zero-cost Options are first-class** — a free optional Ryder Cup is just a $0 Option (yes/no). All Optional contests route through #216.

One thing this sharpens that's worth keeping in view: **changing a contest's reconciliation changes its lane**, so moving a contest *into* Trip Cost should enroll current attendees (#215), and moving it *out* to an Option flips it to opt-in — a transition I've parked with #216/#217 since it involves un-enrolling people who didn't opt in. Flagged it in #215 so it's not forgotten.

Anything else to refine on the model, or should I leave the three issues staged and ready to build when you are?

Here's a scenario that happened this past year:

I registered for the full event.  On Friday morning, I discovered that my son was accepted to perform in an event on Saturday morning.  So I had to leave Friday before an evening cornhole tournament, and missed the entire Saturday contests.  We can't be too sticky on the rules.  A participant needs to be able to be added and removed from a contest regardless of their enrollment status.  We might have someone local drive in just to play in the Saturday round, but otherwise not stay at the hotel, or participate in the other contests.  Does that make sense?

Yes, that makes complete sense — and it's a crucial principle I had too rigid. The takeaway: **contest participation is its own source of truth, independent of event attendance.** Attendance only *seeds* participation (auto-enroll for Included contests); it never constrains it. Concretely:

- **Attending but not in a contest** (you, leaving Friday) — you stay on the roster, but get pulled from Friday cornhole + all Saturday contests.
- **In a contest but not attending** (the local drop-in) — added to just the Saturday round, never on the full roster, never paid trip cost.
- **Edits are never blocked.** "Can't be too sticky" means the system *informs* about consequences (empty team seat), it doesn't *refuse* the change.

And it has a money consequence the ledger handles cleanly: trip cost is charged to the roster, but per-contest divergences get reconciled through the ledger — a one-off charge for the drop-in's round, or a credit for your missed Saturday. That's exactly what v1's manual/adjustment/credit transaction sources are for.

Let me fold this into the issues — it changes #215 (participation ≠ attendance) and meaningfully softens #217 (inform, don't block).

## Behavior (mirror v1's split, then alert)

**Member drops their own RSVP** (likelihood < 99 via `/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`): honor reality — they're not coming. Hard-cascade them off teams, blanket contests, and paid options (reversing those charges). This matches v1's `cascadeRemoveFromRoster`. **New:** fire an admin alert for every contest where the removal left a hole (empty team seat, etc.).

**Admin toggles someone off** (admin attendance write): **guarded** removal — refuse to silently orphan protected state (on a scramble team, has a tee time, is a recorded winner, has a Calcutta bid when that lands). Remove from unprotected contests, return warnings for the protected ones, and alert so the admin can unwind by hand. Matches v1's `protectedContests`.

In both paths the member leaves the event roster; the difference is how aggressively protected contest state is torn down vs. preserved-with-warning.
input.new_string:
## Behavior: never block — detect, remove, and inform

Hard rule (from the "can't be too sticky" principle in #215): **no attendance change or participation edit is ever refused**, even when it breaks downstream state. "Integrity" here means *detect and surface* breakage (and offer cleanup), not *prevent* it. This is a deliberate departure from v1, which refused guarded removals.

**Member drops their own RSVP** (likelihood < 99 via `/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`): honor reality — they're not coming. Cascade them off teams, Included contests, and opted-in Options (reversing those ledger charges). Then **alert admins** for every contest where it left a hole.

**Admin toggles someone off, or edits a single contest's participants** (the common partial case — left early, or a drop-in added to one round): apply the change as requested — **never blocked**. For any contest where it orphans protected state (empty scramble seat, a tee time, a recorded winner, a Calcutta bid when that lands), raise a **warning + admin alert + "needs attention"** flag so a human fixes the team, rather than silently leaving it broken.

The difference between the two paths is only *scope* (full roster leave vs a single-contest edit), not whether removal is allowed — it always is.

=== 00249 cost_items (schema + included_in_trip_cost + source) ===
-- v2 financial management (#213). cost_items is the single source of truth for
-- every dollar in an event (contest buy-ins, lodging, meals, shirts, option fees).
-- Each item reconciles to exactly one bucket: the Trip Cost (included_in_trip_cost,
-- folded into the base price everyone pays), an Option (linked_option_id, opt-in),
-- or neither (operational / pass-through, tracked but not charged).
--
-- Amount lives HERE — cost-bearing things (contests, side games, …) point at a
-- cost_item via source_type/source_id rather than storing their own amount.
--
-- RLS: permissive at the DB; writes are admin-gated in the API (mirrors the rest
-- of v2). Members may read, but the UI never shows the breakdown to non-admins.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.v2_cost_items CASCADE;

CREATE TABLE public.v2_cost_items (
  id                    UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id                UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.v2_organizations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  event_id              UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.v2_events(id)        ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name                  TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_cents          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  category              TEXT,          -- contest | side_game | lodging | food | shirts | operational | pass_through | other
  included_in_trip_cost BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  linked_option_id      UUID,          -- → v2_options once that lands (phase 3); plain UUID for now
  source_type           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',  -- manual | contest | side_game | lodging | …
  source_id             UUID,          -- the owning row (e.g. the contest); NULL for manual
  sort_order            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  notes                 TEXT,
  created_by            UUID REFERENCES public.v2_profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_v2_cost_items_event ON public.v2_cost_items(event_id, sort_order);
CREATE INDEX idx_v2_cost_items_source ON public.v2_cost_items(source_type, source_id) WHERE source_id IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE public.v2_cost_items ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "v2_cost_items_all" ON public.v2_cost_items FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE public.v2_cost_items TO authenticated, service_role;

-- 00252_v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions.sql
-- Opt-out tombstone for contest enrollment (#215, epic #214). Ports v1's
-- contest_enrollment_exclusions (migration 00165).
--
-- Why: Included contests (v2_contests.auto_enroll=true) auto-enroll every on-roster
-- member. When an admin deliberately pulls one person from such a contest — e.g. a
-- member who attended but left early and can't play Saturday's round — we must NOT
-- silently re-add them on the next attendance sync. This table records that explicit
-- removal so the additive enroll skips them until they're explicitly re-added (which
-- clears the tombstone). Distinct from a full roster leave.
--
-- Participation is independent of attendance: a member stays on_roster while being
-- excluded from a specific contest.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions CASCADE;

CREATE TABLE public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions (
  id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  contest_id  UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.v2_contests(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.v2_profiles(id)  ON DELETE CASCADE,
  removed_by  UUID REFERENCES public.v2_profiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  reason      TEXT,
  removed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE (contest_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_v2_contest_exclusions_user ON public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions(user_id);

-- Permissive RLS, API-gated writes (mirrors the rest of the v2 contest tables).
ALTER TABLE public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "v2_contest_exclusions_all" ON public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions
  FOR ALL TO authenticated USING (true) WITH CHECK (true);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE public.v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions
  TO authenticated, service_role;

#215 is built — typecheck, lint, and production build all pass. Here's what shipped and how to verify it.

## What I built (#215)

**The root cause of your "0 players":** v2 already had a `v2_contests.auto_enroll` flag and auto-enroll logic — but it only ran at contest **create** time. You created "Round 1" *before* marking anyone attending, so it enrolled an empty roster, and nothing re-enrolled the 41 when they became attending later. So I didn't need a new flag — I needed the missing triggers and manual controls.

- **Migration `00252_v2_contest_enrollment_exclusions`** — the opt-out tombstone table.
- **`src/lib/v2/contests/enrollment.ts`** — `syncAttendanceEnrollment` (enroll on attend), `enrollRosterIntoContest` (import all), `add`/`removeContestParticipants` (with tombstones). Participation is authoritative and independent of attendance, per your scenario.
- **Participants write API** — `POST` (import-all or add specific members, including non-attendees) and `DELETE` (remove + tombstone) on the contest participants route, admin-gated.
- **Triggers wired:** RSVP → "Attending" now auto-enrolls into all auto-enroll contests; flipping a contest's `auto_enroll` on pulls in the current roster.
- **"Add players" UI** on the contest page — a Players section with **"Add everyone attending (N)"**, a searchable subset picker (with an "attending" tag, but *any* member addable — the local drop-in), and per-player **Remove** (ConfirmModal; they stay on the roster but won't be auto-re-added).

## To use it

1. **Apply migration `00252`** (same way you ran 251).
2. Reload the **Round 1** contest page → click **"Add everyone attending (41)"** → it'll show 41 players. That fixes your current event immediately.

- **Early-leaver:** Remove a player → confirm → they vanish from the contest but are still Attending the event; re-running "Add everyone attending" does **not** re-add them (tombstone holds) until you add them back explicitly.
- **Not blocked:** removing someone never errors, even mid-setup.

## 1. Generate Teams now has real math (A/B/C/D snake draft)
`doGenerate()` was a random shuffle. It now:
1. Sorts participants by handicap, low → high (players with no handicap on file sort last, treated as highest).
2. Deals them one tier at a time into `numTeams` teams, **reversing direction each tier** (serpentine).

Result: every team gets exactly one player from each quartile (A/B/C/D), and the snake ordering keeps total team strength balanced. Verified on your live Round 1 data:

```
Team 1: [2.0, 15.2, 16.6, 31.6]  sum=65.4
Team 5: [4.8, 12.0, 19.8, 28.4]  sum=65.0
Team 10:[8.4,  9.8, 23.4, 24.8]  sum=66.4
Team-sum spread: 63.6 to 66.4   ← across 10 teams
```

It respects the 2/3/4-man size selector (tiers = team size, so a 3-man generates A/B/C). It's deterministic now (same handicaps → same optimal teams), which is the point of a seeded draft — but you can still hand-tweak after.

## 2. Handicaps seeded
All 50 fake members got a handicap index (spread **2.0 to 31.6**, non-monotonic so quartiles are meaningful), via `scripts/seed-tko-handicaps.mjs` (idempotent, touches only the fake members — your real handicap is untouched). This also makes the existing **"Auto handicaps"** button work.

## To see it
Round 1 → **Teams** → pick a size → **Generate teams**. You'll get balanced A/B/C/D teams instead of random ones.

One note: a participant with **no** handicap (e.g. you, the owner, if you're enrolled — I only seeded the fakes) is treated as the highest handicap and lands in the last tier. If you want yourself drafted realistically, give the owner account a handicap too and I can extend the script.

I noticed that when generating teams with 41 players, we end up with 3 three-player teams.  I suppose that seems correct.  We never allow 5-player teams.

Correct — that's exactly the intended behavior, and it's guaranteed by the math, not luck.

With 41 players at 4-man teams: `numTeams = ceil(41 / 4) = 11`. The snake draft deals players round-robin across those 11 teams, so every team ends up with either `floor(41/11)=3` or `ceil(41/11)=4` players. Since `numTeams` is always `ceil(players / teamSize)`, the max possible team size is exactly `teamSize` and the remainder teams get **one fewer**, never one more. So:

- **41 players, 4-man** → 11 teams: 8 fours + 3 threes ✅
- **A 5-player team is mathematically impossible** at that size — you'd need `numTeams` to be too small, and `ceil` prevents that.

One detail you may or may not care about: the three short (3-player) teams are currently always the **top-seeded** teams (teams 1–3, the ones holding the lowest-handicap A players). That falls out of the serpentine — the final partial tier (the D players) gets dealt in reverse and runs out before it reaches the first few teams. It's arguably fine (a 3-strong-player scramble team isn't exactly disadvantaged), but if you'd rather the short teams be spread differently — or always be the *weaker* teams — that's a small tweak to which end the last tier fills from.

**Slice 1 of #216 is built** (typecheck, lint, build all pass). Checking in before I go further, since the rest builds on this foundation and on a model decision.

## The model decision (worth confirming)
I went with **derived charges** instead of v1's store-every-charge ledger:
- **Charges derive live** — Trip Cost (if on-roster) + each selected option's *current* price (sum of its bundled cost_items). Edit a cost_item → everything re-prices automatically, nothing goes stale. This is the one deviation from v1, and it eliminates v1's read-time re-pricing complexity.
- **The ledger stores only what you can't derive** — payments, credits, manual charges, adjustments (covers your drop-in's à-la-carte charge and the early-leaver's credit).
- **Balance = derived charges + manual charges − payments.**

Still "mirror v1" in spirit (a real ledger for the un-derivable money), just cleaner.

## What's built (slice 1 — admin option management)
- **Migration `00253`** — `v2_options`, `v2_user_option_selections`, `v2_financial_transactions`.
- **Options admin page** (event admin → **Options** tile, now wired): create options, bundle contests/costs into each (reusing the existing cost_items reconcile, so bundling an item auto-removes it from Trip Cost), **derived price** per option, edit/delete. Plus an "unassigned costs" section surfacing anything not in Trip Cost and not in an option.

## To try it
Apply **migration `00253`**, then event admin → **Options**: add an option like "Closest to the Pin," and bundle contest buy-ins into it to watch the price sum up.

## What's next
- **Slice 2:** member-facing selection (pick options) + the option→contest enrollment sync (selecting enrolls into all bundled contests; here I'll also handle **free options**, which need $0 cost_items to bundle) + ledger wiring for payments.
- **Slice 3:** balances — member "what you owe" (Trip Cost + options as single lines) and admin per-member reconcile.

-- 00254_v2_cost_categories.sql
-- Platform-managed reference data: cost-item categories (#216 follow-up). Moves the
-- hardcoded category list (src/lib/v2/cost-items.ts) into a table that SYSTEM ADMINS
-- manage from the platform console (/new/admin). First resident of a general
-- "platform data management" area (GH #178 system-admin tier). Group-level overrides
-- can layer on later; this is the shared default set.
--
-- cost_items.category stays a plain TEXT key (no FK, backward compatible); this table
-- supplies the human label + emoji icon for display and the pick list.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.v2_cost_categories CASCADE;
CREATE TABLE public.v2_cost_categories (
  id         UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  key        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,     -- stable slug stored on cost_items.category
  label      TEXT NOT NULL,            -- display name
  icon       TEXT,                     -- emoji, rendered inline (works in native <select>)
  sort_order INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  is_active  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

INSERT INTO public.v2_cost_categories (key, label, icon, sort_order) VALUES
  ('lodging',      'Lodging',      '🏨', 0),
  ('food',         'Food',         '🍽️', 1),
  ('shirts',       'Shirts',       '👕', 2),
  ('operational',  'Operational',  '⚙️', 3),
  ('pass_through', 'Pass-through', '🔁', 4),
  ('other',        'Other',        '🏷️', 5)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- Platform reference data: everyone may READ (needed to render labels); only the
-- service-role client WRITES (the API gates those on isSystemAdmin). No write policy
-- for authenticated, so a hand-rolled client can't mutate platform data.
ALTER TABLE public.v2_cost_categories ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "v2_cost_categories_read" ON public.v2_cost_categories FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);

GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.v2_cost_categories TO authenticated;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE public.v2_cost_categories TO service_role;

content.text:
**Slice 2 of #216 is done** — typecheck, lint, and build all pass. Members can now opt into options, which enrolls them into the bundled contests (filling those 0s).

## What's built
- **Option → contest enrollment sync** (`syncOptionContestEnrollment`): selecting an option enrolls the member into *every* contest it bundles; deselecting removes them from all. All-or-nothing, idempotent.
- **Member selection API** — `POST`/`DELETE /api/v2/events/[eventId]/options/[optionId]/selection` (acts on the member themselves, membership-gated).
- **Member-facing Options module** on the event home (right after RSVP): each option as a single line — name, description, price (or **"Free"**) — with a fillable check toggle. Shows the **Trip Cost** line when you're attending, and a derived **"Your total"** at the bottom. Members never see the contests inside a bundle (per #125).

## To see the full loop
1. Event admin → **Options** → create an option (e.g. "Closest to the Pin") and bundle the CTP side games' costs into it.
2. On the event **home**, the Options module appears → toggle the option on.
3. Back on the **Contests** page, those side games' player counts tick up from 0 — because selecting enrolled you into them.

## One known gap (flagged for later)
Free contests currently have **no cost_item** (we delete it at $0), and options bundle *through* cost_items — so a free optional contest can't be bundled yet. That research is gold — and you're right, option creation in v1 is a whole subsystem, not a cost-item assignment. My v2 slice-1 only built the simplest corner of it. Here's the honest picture.

## What v1 option authoring actually is

It's an **option-first builder** (`OptionBuilder.tsx`, ~1,500 lines), structured as **Groups → Options → Choices**, with cost-items linked *into* it (not the other way around, which is how I approached v2):

- **Groups** (`option_groups`) — collapsible sections ("Contest Entry Fees", "Lodging"), with their own icon + order.
- **7 option types** — `checkbox`, `select` (one-of), `multi_select` (many-of), `quantity` (counters w/ `max_total`), `text`, `number`, and the special derived `trip_cost`.
- **Choices** (JSONB) for select/multi_select/quantity — each choice has its own **label, cost, and contest link**. "Lodging?" → "Mon & Tue ($200) / Tue only ($100) / None (free)" is one `select` option with three choices, each priced and optionally enrolling into a different contest.
- **Per-choice cost linking** via a `cost_item_option_choices` junction (which cost_item funds *which choice*), not just a whole-option link.
- **Dependencies** (`depends_on_option_id`) — "What shirt size?" only appears if "T-shirt" is selected; deselecting the parent clears the child.
- **`is_required`**, **`max_total`**, an **~80-icon picker** (on groups *and* options), **markdown descriptions**, **drag-reorder at all three levels**, and a **selection deadline + open/closed** setting.

## The gap vs. what I built

My v2 slice-1 = **one `checkbox` option whose price is the sum of bundled cost_items**. That happens to nail your CTP example ($15 = 6 × $2.50). But it can't express:
- Lodging (`select` with priced choices)
- KGB Cup add-ons (`multi_select`)
- Extra shirts (`quantity` + max)
- Dietary notes (`text`)
- Conditional/required options, groups, icons, per-choice contest enrollment, or the open/closed deadline.

And architecturally, v1 links cost **per choice**; my v2 links a cost_item to a whole option. To do select/multi_select faithfully I need the per-choice junction (`v2_cost_item_option_choices`) — which I haven't built.

## My recommendation

This is bigger than "finish #216 slice 2/3" — it's effectively a **rebuild of v2 options to mirror v1's OptionBuilder**, and it should be its own tracked effort. I'd phase it: **(A)** groups + checkbox/select/multi_select + choices + icons + required + markdown + drag order; **(B)** per-choice cost + contest linking; **(C)** quantity/text/number + dependencies + deadline/open-closed.

Before I write any of that up or touch code, one scoping call is yours:

# v2: option authoring — full v1 parity (OptionBuilder rebuild)

Part of #214, expands #216. The options work in #216 shipped the simplest corner only (one `checkbox` option whose price = sum of bundled cost_items). v1's option authoring is a full subsystem (`OptionBuilder.tsx`, ~1,500 lines) structured **Groups → Options → Choices** with per-choice cost + contest linking, dependencies, 7 types, icons, and an open/closed deadline. This issue rebuilds v2 options to mirror it. Decision (2026-10-01): **full v1 parity, rebuild to v1 shape** — slice-1's cost-bundling becomes the `checkbox` case.

## The v1 model we're matching
`option_groups` (sections) → `trip_options` (7 types) → `choices` (JSONB, per-choice cost + contest). Cost-items link *into* options (per choice via `cost_item_option_choices`), not the reverse. Plus dependencies, required/limits, icons, markdown, drag-order at 3 levels, and a selection deadline + open/closed. Reference: `src/components/admin/OptionBuilder.tsx`, `CostItemLinksModal.tsx`, `src/lib/option-icons.tsx`, `src/lib/cost-items/compute.ts`, `option-contest-sync.ts`, migrations `00071/00072/00073/00076/00115/00138/00139/00146-7`.

## Schema (rebuild to v1 shape)

**`v2_option_groups`** (new) — `id, org_id, event_id, name, description, icon, sort_order`.

**`v2_options`** (expand) — add:
- `group_id UUID → v2_option_groups`
- `option_type` CHECK → `checkbox | select | multi_select | quantity | text | number | trip_cost`
- `choices JSONB` — `[{label, value, cost?, contest_id?}]` (value auto-slugged from label)
- `is_required BOOLEAN`, `max_total INTEGER` (quantity cap)
- `icon TEXT`, `depends_on_option_id UUID → v2_options`
- keep `name, description (markdown), sort_order`

**`v2_cost_item_option_choices`** (new junction) — `cost_item_id, choice_value` (which cost_item funds which choice). Empty rows → applies to the whole option (checkbox) / default.

**`v2_user_option_selections`** (expand) — add `value JSONB` (true | "choiceValue" | ["v1","v2"] | {choice: qty}); presence alone is no longer enough for multi-choice types.

**`v2_event_option_settings`** (new) — `event_id PK, selection_deadline, is_open`.

## Pricing + enrollment (per type)
- **Price derivation** (ports `compute.ts`): checkbox = SUM(linked cost_items with no choice rows); select/multi_select/quantity = per-choice SUM of cost_items matching that choice via the junction; quantity total = Σ(choice cost × qty); `trip_cost` = SUM(included_in_trip_cost).
- **Contest enrollment** (ports `option-contest-sync.ts`): selecting a choice enrolls into the contests whose funding cost_items map to that choice value (per-choice), plus any whole-option link. Deselect removes.
- Member charges stay **derived** (the #216 decision) from selections × current prices; the ledger still stores only payments/manual.

## Admin UI — OptionBuilder (ports `OptionBuilder.tsx`)
A dedicated builder at `/new/[slug]/admin/events/[eventId]/options`:
- **Settings bar**: selection deadline + Open/Closed toggle.
- **Groups**: add/rename/icon/delete, drag-reorder, collapse/expand.
- **Option form** (per option): name, icon picker, markdown description, **type dropdown** (7), **choices editor** (drag-reorder rows; label auto-slugs value; cost read-only "derived from linked cost items"; delete/add), `max_total` (quantity only), **Required** toggle, **Depends on…** picker, Save/Delete.
- **Cost-item linking modal** (ports `CostItemLinksModal.tsx`): per-choice toggles mapping cost_items → choices, with running per-choice totals; items linked elsewhere greyed.
- Drag-reorder at group / option / choice levels.
- **Icon library** (port `option-icons.tsx`, ~80 icons / 11 categories) shared by groups + options.

## Member UI (ports the member selection render)
Render each type on the event home Options module: checkbox toggle, select (radio/dropdown), multi_select (checklist), quantity (steppers w/ max), text/number inputs, trip_cost (read-only line). Respect groups, required, dependencies (hide child until parent selected; clear on deselect), and open/closed (lock when closed/past deadline). One line per option with its price; never the contests inside.

## Phases
- **A — structure + core types**: schema (groups, types, choices, deps, required, icon, settings), OptionBuilder (groups + option form + choices editor + icon picker + markdown + drag order), member render for checkbox/select/multi_select. Whole-option cost (slice-1 behavior) still works.
- **B — per-choice cost + contest linking**: `v2_cost_item_option_choices` + CostItemLinksModal + per-choice price derivation + per-choice contest enrollment.
- **C — advanced**: quantity (+max_total) & text/number types, `depends_on_option_id` cascade, selection deadline + open/closed enforcement.

## Migration note
Rework `v2_options` in place (it only has slice-1 test data). `v2_user_option_selections` gains `value` (default `'true'` for existing checkbox rows).

## Non-goals (for now)
Audience/visibility targeting on options (reuse announcements model later if needed); member-specific admin-set options.

content.text:
**#218 is complete — full v1 parity for option authoring**, all verified (typecheck, lint, build green). Here's everything that landed in this push:

## Phase B — per-choice cost + contest linking
- `v2_cost_item_option_choices` junction; the cost-item link endpoint now takes `choice_values`.
- The admin **"Add cost"** modal has a **"Funds which choice?"** picker; bundled items show a choice badge.
- Per-choice price derivation (`loadOptionChoicePrices` → whole + per-choice); member **pills/steppers show each choice's price**, and "Your total" uses the real per-choice charge.
- Enrollment is now **per-choice**: selecting a choice enrolls you only into the contests that choice funds.

## Phase C — dependencies cascade + open/closed deadline
- Deselecting an option **cascades** to clear everything that depends on it (recursive, server-side, with enrollment cleanup).
- `v2_event_option_settings`: admin **settings bar** (Open toggle + Selection deadline). When closed/past deadline, members are **locked out** (controls disabled, "Options are closed" note) and the API rejects member changes (admins bypass).

## Trip Cost as the unremovable, depended-on option (your ask)
- Every event auto-gets one special **Trip Cost** option (`option_type='trip_cost'`).
- Admin: a **pinned, non-deletable Trip Cost card** (price derived from Financials); the depends-on picker offers **"Trip Cost (requires attending)"**, and **new options default to depending on it**.
- Member: Trip Cost shows as the always-present unremovable line; any option depending on it is **only selectable when you're attending** — exactly "you can't get into contests/options unless you're paying for the trip."

## To try it
Event admin → **Options**: you'll see the Trip Cost card + settings bar. Add a "Select one" lodging option, bundle a cost per choice, and it defaults to depending on Trip Cost. On the home, a non-attending member sees Trip Cost + a "RSVP to join" note with options hidden; attending members get the full picker.

## One honest gap
When a member **drops their RSVP**, the member UI hides their Trip-Cost-dependent options, but the stored selections/enrollments aren't auto-cleared yet — that's **#217's attendance cascade** (still unbuilt). Flagged in memory.

No migration needed beyond `00255` (already applied); `ensureTripCostOption` creates the row on first admin visit. Want me to tackle that #217 attendance-cascade gap next, or test the option builder first?

Options definitely shouldn't be shown directly on the home page.  IF options are open, a box should appear on the home page reminding users to complete their options.  Clicking the button should bring up a modal that walks the user through each individual choice.

Here's how we manage the different states of options:

0. Options closed: don't show anything on the home page or "everything" menu.
1. Options open, choices incomplete: show the button on the home page, with a pulse. Options also show up in the "Everything" menu.
2. Options open, choices complete: show the button, no pulse.  Allows users to update their choices before the close date. Options also show up in the "Everything" menu.
3. Options open, but expiration has passed. Home page button disappears. Options also show up in the "Everything" menu, but the options are read-only.

Both requests are in and verified (typecheck, lint, build green; migration 256 applied).

## Options moved off the home → reminder + wizard
- **Home no longer lists options.** When options are open, it shows a single **reminder button** that **pulses while any required option is unanswered** ("Complete your options") and goes solid once done ("Your options" — still editable before the deadline).
- Clicking it opens a **wizard modal** that walks through **each option one at a time** (per-type control), ending in a **summary + Your total**.
- The **full list** lives on a member **Options page** reached from the **"Everything" menu** (I injected the entry, replacing the old `my_options` stub).

### The state machine you specified (now with a scheduled-open state)
| State | Home button | Everything menu |
|---|---|---|
| Closed (`is_open` off) | — | — |
| **Scheduled** (before open date) | — | — |
| Open, incomplete | **button + pulse** | editable |
| Open, complete | button, no pulse | editable |
| Open, past deadline | — | **read-only** |

## Scheduled open date + auto-open + authored notification
- `v2_event_option_settings` gained **`selection_open_at`** plus **authored notification** fields (migration 256).
- Admin **Availability** panel now has **Opens / Closes** datetimes and an **Opening notification** (title + body).
- Opening is **automatic** (time-gated — no button needed), and a **cron** (`/api/cron/v2-options-open`, every minute, registered in `vercel.json`) fires the authored notification to members the moment options open, deep-linking to the options page. It claims a one-time `sent_at` tombstone so it never double-sends; rescheduling the open re-arms it.

This start+end-window + authored-notification setup is built to be the **template** for the other time-gated things you mentioned.

Event admin → **Options** → set **Opens** a minute out, add an **Opening notification**, keep **Open for selections** on. Before the open time: nothing on home/menu. After it passes (cron runs): members get the push, the home reminder appears (pulsing if they've got required options), and the Options page shows in Everything.

You nailed it. The infra's already there — I just duplicated it:

- **Availability windows already exist on features**: `availability: "always" | "window"` + `available_from` / `available_until` on `v2_event_features`, and the `/features` PUT API already accepts them. `lockReasonFor()` already produces "Opens Mar 3" / "Closed" / active — literally your states 0–3.
- So **`v2_event_option_settings` was a parallel reinvention** of what Features does. It should go.
- The **only genuinely new thing** is the *authored "it's now open" notification* — Features doesn't have that yet. That's the piece worth generalizing to all features.

What's missing today: the Features admin screen fetches the window fields but has **no UI to edit them** — so "apply start dates to all features" is mostly a UI + a general notification, not new plumbing.

## The refactor
1. **Delete the options-specific scheduling** — the two accordions, `v2_event_option_settings` gating, and my custom launcher injection. Options becomes a normal feature (routed to `/options`), turned on/scheduled in **Features** like everything else.
2. **Member gating derives from the resolved feature state**: active (within window) → editable + the home reminder; past `available_until` ("Closed") → read-only in the menu; off / before start → nothing. (The reminder + wizard stay options-specific UX — they just read the feature's active state.)
3. **Build the per-feature window editor** in the Features admin screen (availability toggle + Opens/Closes datetimes). The API already takes it.
4. **Generalize the authored open-notification to all features** — move `open_notification_title/body/sent_at` onto `v2_event_features`, add it to the Features editor, and one general cron fires it when any feature's `available_from` passes (replacing the options-specific cron).

One nuance: `v2_event_option_settings` currently also powers the server-side selection lock + the member read-only. Those just re-point at the feature's resolved window — same logic, different source.

Yes — that resolves it cleanly, and it's the right distinction:

- **Features owns *visibility* + the *start/open* date** (and the "it's open" notification) — "can users access this feature, and when does it appear." Generic to every feature.
- **Options owns its *close* date** — the read-only cutoff where the feature stays visible but selection stops. That's unique to Options (most features don't have a "visible but frozen" state), so it belongs on the Options page.

So I'll undo my "remove everything" direction on the Options page and keep **only the close date** there, while visibility/start/notification live in Features. Let me correct course.
