This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The overarching session goal is building out the Golfapalooza v2 platform (`/new`), mirroring the mature v1 app feature-by-feature. Discrete intents in chronological order:
   - Set up an isolated test group/event (user created "TKO Trivia" group + "TKO Trivia XXXI" event).
   - Build a master-admin "all groups" view (system-admin tier, GH #178) — user chose "Full v1 parity" + "Rebuild to v1 shape" where asked, and "bootstrap via phone" (`6143275066` → `+16143275066`), "View + manage" scope.
   - Populate test data: 40 fake members, mark all attending, add 10 non-attending, give all handicaps, give all unique nicknames.
   - Fix: event end-date picker should default to start-date's month; org orange color should theme the whole site; skins scoring tile overflow; scoring card should show net/handicap/score in large font (and show 0s before holes played — "These are admin tools. We want to see what is happening"); article placeholder should only show after first article published.
   - Design + build the enrollment/money/attendance-integrity system (epic #214 → #215/#216/#217). Decisions: options are the member-facing money unit, all-or-nothing, can bundle multiple contests; "Trip Cost is one big option" (derived); mirror v1's ledger but with DERIVED charges (not stored, to avoid re-pricing complexity); participation is INDEPENDENT of attendance ("we can't be too sticky on the rules," admins add/remove anyone from any contest regardless of RSVP).
   - #215 (shipped): attendance→contest auto-enroll + Players tab (grouped In/Not-in checklist, preset buttons, drag, opt-out tombstones).
   - Teams: "generate teams" should do A/B/C/D snake draft by handicap; show handicap on player pills.
   - #216 Options: build to FULL v1 PARITY (user was emphatic: "You've still missed meaningful details... Each 'option' was an accordion, with the details inside. They were re-orderable. Please please please be detail oriented"). Covers: groups, 7 option types, choices with per-choice cost/contest, dependencies, required, icons, open/close scheduling.
   - Trip Cost as an unremovable option that all other options depend on ("you can't get into a contest unless you're also paying for the trip").
   - Member UX redesign: "Options definitely shouldn't be shown directly on the home page" → a reminder box/button (pulse when incomplete) opening a wizard that walks through each choice; full list in "Everything" menu; 4 states (closed/open-incomplete/open-complete/expired-read-only).
   - Scheduled OPEN date (not just close) with auto-open + authored notification at open moment ("first of many things that could have both a start and end date").
   - Make opening-notification + open/close dates collapsible accordions.
   - **MOST RECENT CRITICAL PIVOT**: "I don't love this paradigm. We already have a place (Features) to toggle whether certain modules are visible... remove this from the Options page directly, and apply this new model (start dates) to all features. Options can be turned on there, like everything else." Confirmed: "Yes, do the full refactor" + "Generalize to all features now."

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Next.js 16 App Router, Supabase (Postgres), v2 platform under `src/app/new/` with `v2_`-prefixed tables, RLS permissive + API-gated writes.
   - Feature registry (`src/lib/v2/features.ts`): FeatureDef catalog, resolveFeatures (catalog < org < event), buildEventNav (pinned + launcher), FeatureAvailability ("always"|"window") with available_from/available_until, lockReasonFor ("Opens X"/"Closed"/null), isFeatureActive, FEATURE_ROUTES map, featureHref.
   - Options model: Groups → Options (7 types: checkbox/select/multi_select/quantity/text/number/trip_cost) → Choices (JSONB {label,value,cost?,contest_id?}), per-choice cost via `v2_cost_item_option_choices` junction, dependencies (depends_on_option_id), derived pricing (loadOptionChoicePrices, priceForValue).
   - Derived-charge money model: charges derived from selections × current cost_item prices; ledger (`v2_financial_transactions`) stores only payments/manual/credits.
   - dnd-kit for drag-reorder (DndContext, SortableContext, useSortable, arrayMove).
   - Cron pattern: Bearer CRON_SECRET auth + v2AdminClient + atomic tombstone claim; registered in vercel.json.
   - sendV2Notifications(admin, userIds[], {orgId, type, title, body?, data?}).
   - Emoji icons (not SVG) for cost categories + option icons (consistency, lightweight).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `src/lib/v2/features.ts` (CURRENT WORK) — added notification fields to FeatureRow (`open_notification_title?`, `open_notification_body?`, `open_notification_sent_at?` all optional), ResolvedFeature (`openNotificationTitle: string|null`, `openNotificationBody: string|null`), baseResolved (nulls), applyRow (`openNotificationTitle: row.open_notification_title ?? acc.openNotificationTitle`). Added `featureHasOpened(f, viewerIsAdmin, now)` helper. Added `options: (slug) => \`/new/${slug}/options\`` to FEATURE_ROUTES. Changed registry: `my_options` (planned) → `{ key: "options", label: "Options", bucket: "schedule", scope: "event", icon: "list", status: "available", surface: "route", blurb: "Add-ons & extras you opt into." }`.

Still contains the Availability + Opening-notification ACCORDIONS + patchSettings + settings state (TO BE REMOVED per the refactor).

v2 feature scheduling model (#218), finalized after a user pivot away from options-specific scheduling.

**Features registry owns visibility + open date + the "it's open" notification** (generic to every feature). On `v2_event_features`: `availability` ('always'|'window'), `available_from`, `available_until`, plus authored `open_notification_title`/`body`/`sent_at` (migration 00257). Admin UI = `FeaturesConfig.tsx` (per-feature "Scheduling & notification" block). A general cron `/api/cron/v2-feature-open` (every minute, in vercel.json) atomically claims `open_notification_sent_at` and sends a `feature_open` notification when `available_from` passes. The old `v2-options-open` cron was deleted.

**Options owns ONLY its read-only close date** — the one thing unique to Options: after the cutoff the page stays VISIBLE but selections freeze. Lives on `v2_event_option_settings.selection_deadline` (its other columns is_open/selection_open_at/open_notification_* are now dead). `OptionSettings` type + `loadOptionSettings` trimmed to just `selection_deadline`; `selectionsStillOpen(s, nowMs)` replaced `optionsAreOpen`/`optionsHaveOpened`. Admin edits it via one date field on the Options page (OptionsManager) → `option-settings` PUT (selection_deadline only).

Two helpers in `features.ts` encode the split:
- `featureHasOpened(f, isAdmin, now)` = visible + past `available_from` (IGNORES `available_until`) → gates page ACCESS so the read-only state stays reachable.
- `isFeatureActive(f, isAdmin, now)` = visible + within full window → gates EDITABILITY.

Member gating (all AND the close date): `editable = isFeatureActive(optionsFeat) && selectionsStillOpen(settings)`; `accessible = featureHasOpened(optionsFeat)`. ## What changed

**Features owns visibility + open + notification (generic to every feature)**
- `v2_event_features` carries `availability`/`available_from`/`available_until` + authored `open_notification_title`/`body`/`sent_at` (migration 00257, already applied).
- `FeaturesConfig.tsx` has a per-feature "Scheduling & notification" block — set when a feature appears and author its "it's open" push.
- New general cron `/api/cron/v2-feature-open` (every minute) fires that notification the moment any feature's `available_from` passes, atomically claiming `sent_at` so it never double-sends. The old options-only `v2-options-open` cron is deleted and `vercel.json` updated.
- `options` is now a normal routed registry feature; the custom launcher injection is gone from the event layout.

**Options owns ONLY its close date (the read-only cutoff)**
- The Options page keeps a single "Selections close" date field. After it, the page stays visible but picks freeze. Visibility, open date, and the open notification moved to Features — the two scheduling accordions on the Options page are gone.
- `OptionSettings` / `v2_event_option_settings` trimmed to just `selection_deadline` (the old `is_open`/`selection_open_at`/`open_notification_*` columns are now dead but harmless).

**The two-helper split that makes it work**
- `featureHasOpened` (visible + past open, ignores close) → gates page **access**, so the read-only state is reachable.
- `isFeatureActive` + `selectionsStillOpen(close date)` → gates **editability**.
- Applied consistently in the event home (reminder), member options page, and the selection API (admins bypass both).

3. **Close cutoff (read-only)** — set the Options page "Selections close" to the past. Home reminder disappears; the Options page still opens but controls are read-only; the selection API returns 403 for members, succeeds for admins.
4. **Off** — set Options visibility off in Features: no reminder, member page redirects, not in the "Everything" menu.
5. **Other features** — pick any windowed feature (e.g. Articles), author a notification + future open date, confirm the same general cron fires its push.

## The good news: no schema change needed

The model **already supports** one cost item funding multiple choices — `v2_cost_item_option_choices` is a many-to-many junction (one cost item ↔ many choice values), the pricing math sums per-choice, the PATCH route already takes a `choice_values` **array**, and even the contest-enrollment sync enrolls when *any* funded choice is picked. The whole thing was being throttled by an authoring UI that assumed one choice per cost.

## What I changed (UI only)

**Admin "Add cost" modal** — the single-select "Funds which choice?" dropdown is now a **checkbox list** with All / None buttons. Tick the choices a cost applies to; leave all off to charge it on every choice. The same cost can now go on several choices at once.

**Placed costs** now show a **badge per funded choice** (or "Every choice"), plus a new **"Choices"** button to edit which choices an already-bundled cost funds, without removing and re-adding.

**Option header price** now shows a **range** (e.g. `$150–$450`) for choice options, since the cost depends on which choice the member picks — the old single sum was misleading (it added up *every* choice's costs, which nobody pays).

**Loader + types** — the admin page now reads *all* junction rows per item (`choice_values: string[]`) instead of keeping only the first.

**Member side: zero changes.** The per-choice pills already read `price_info.byChoice[value]`, so a Monday-night cost attached to all three Monday choices automatically shows up in each of their prices.

Your exact scenario works: create the arrival option with per-day choices, add "Monday hotel night" with all three Monday choices ticked, add "Monday dinner" with only the first two ticked, and so on. Each choice's price (and contest enrollment, if any) derives correctly.

`tsc`, eslint, and `npm run build` all pass.

1. **Multi-choice add** — Options → an arrival-type select option → Add cost → tick several choices → pick "Monday hotel night." It lands once, badged with each chosen choice.
2. **Subset** — add "Monday dinner" with only the first two choices ticked; confirm only those two badges appear.
3. **Edit choices** — click "Choices" on a placed cost, change the set, Save; badges update.
4. **Price range** — the option header shows min–max; a choice with more bundled costs reads higher.
5. **Member view** — open the member Options page/wizard; each choice pill shows its own total (including shared costs like the Monday night); picking one charges exactly that choice's sum.
6. **Contest bundle** (if a funded cost is a contest buy-in) — selecting a choice that funds it enrolls the member; switching to a choice that doesn't un-enrolls.
7. **Whole-option** — add a cost with no choices ticked; confirm it reads "Every choice" and is added to every choice's price.

content.text:
Done. I replaced the confusing "pick-and-consume" modal with a persistent per-choice matrix for choice options (select / multi-select / quantity).

## What it does now

Inside a choice option's editor, under **"Costs by choice,"** every assignable cost item stays listed — both the ones already in use *and* the unassigned pool — grouped by source (contest / category). Each cost is a row with:
- its name + amount
- a wrapping row of **toggle chips, one per choice** (filled = this cost applies to that choice)
- an **All / Clear** shortcut for the flat-fee-on-everything case

Tapping chips is the whole interaction. **Nothing ever disappears** — a cost with no chips lit just sits there, muted; light up ≥1 chip and the row gets a subtle brand tint so "in use" is obvious. Clearing all chips unlinks it (back to the pool) but it stays on screen.

For your arrival option: "Monday hotel night" is one row — tap the three Monday choices (and any later-day ones who still get that night); "Monday dinner" — tap only the first two; and so on down the list. Each cost is visible and editable the whole time, no re-opening modals, no hunting for a vanished item.

Behind the scenes it uses the same many-to-many junction, so pricing, member per-choice prices, and contest enrollment all keep working — this was purely a UI change. Non-choice options (checkbox / number / text) keep the simple add/remove list since there's nothing per-choice to manage.

tsc, eslint, and the production build all pass.

## Verification checklist

1. **Persistence** — open the arrival option; every unassigned cost and every already-bundled cost shows in "Costs by choice," grouped. Light up a chip; the item stays put (doesn't jump to a separate "bundled" list).
2. **One cost, many choices** — tap several Monday choices on "Monday hotel night"; all stay lit; the row tints active.
3. **Subset** — "Monday dinner" lit on only the first two Monday choices; confirm the others stay off.
4. **All / Clear** — "All" lights every choice; "Clear" empties it and un-tints the row (cost returns to the unassigned pool but remains visible).
5. **Price range** — the collapsed option header shows a min–max (e.g. `$0–$73`) reflecting the per-choice totals.
6. **Member side** — open the member Options wizard; each arrival choice's price matches the sum of the costs whose chip you lit for it.
7. **Non-choice untouched** — a checkbox/number option still shows "Bundled costs" + the Add-cost modal.

Also, there's an options container holding all of the options.  We don't need the outer box.  As we add groups, it can just be a small header.  Trying to maximize the width I have available to manage options.

input.content:
-- 00258_v2_dedupe_trip_cost.sql
-- Fix the Trip Cost pileup: ensureTripCostOption used .maybeSingle(), which returns
-- null when >1 row matches, so once two Trip Cost options existed it inserted a new one
-- on every page load (the admin UI hid them behind a neq('trip_cost') filter until that
-- filter was removed). This collapses the duplicates to one per event (keeping the
-- earliest), repoints any option that depended on a doomed Trip Cost to the survivor
-- (depends_on_option_id is ON DELETE SET NULL, so we must repoint BEFORE deleting), and
-- adds a partial unique index so a second Trip Cost per event can never be created again.
-- v2_user_option_selections.option_id is ON DELETE CASCADE, so stray trip-cost selections
-- (there shouldn't be any — Trip Cost isn't member-selectable) clean up automatically.

-- 1. Repoint dependents to the earliest Trip Cost in their event.
WITH survivor AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (event_id) event_id, id
  FROM public.v2_options
  WHERE option_type = 'trip_cost'
  ORDER BY event_id, created_at ASC
),
doomed AS (
  SELECT o.id, s.id AS survivor_id
  FROM public.v2_options o
  JOIN survivor s ON s.event_id = o.event_id
  WHERE o.option_type = 'trip_cost' AND o.id <> s.id
)
UPDATE public.v2_options dep
SET depends_on_option_id = d.survivor_id, updated_at = NOW()
FROM doomed d
WHERE dep.depends_on_option_id = d.id;

-- 2. Delete the duplicate Trip Cost options (keep the earliest per event).
DELETE FROM public.v2_options o
USING (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (event_id) event_id, id
  FROM public.v2_options
  WHERE option_type = 'trip_cost'
  ORDER BY event_id, created_at ASC
) keep
WHERE o.option_type = 'trip_cost'
  AND o.event_id = keep.event_id
  AND o.id <> keep.id;

-- 3. Guard: at most one Trip Cost option per event, forever.
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS public.idx_v2_options_one_trip_cost;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_v2_options_one_trip_cost
  ON public.v2_options (event_id)
  WHERE option_type = 'trip_cost';

Fixed, and migration 258 is in. Those SQL editor errors are the usual T-SQL false positives (it parses Postgres `DISTINCT ON` / `USING` / CTEs as SQL Server) — safe to ignore, and "258 complete" confirms it ran.

## What happened

`ensureTripCostOption` used `.maybeSingle()`, which returns **null when more than one row matches**. So the moment two Trip Costs existed, every page load saw "null → none exist → insert another." It snowballed to 257. You never noticed because the admin query filtered Trip Cost out (`neq('option_type','trip_cost')`) — and when I removed that filter to make Trip Cost draggable, all the accumulated rows became visible. The bug was pre-existing; my change just unmasked it.

## The fix (all shipped)

1. **Stopped the bleeding** — `ensureTripCostOption` now orders by `created_at` and takes the earliest with `.limit(1)` instead of `.maybeSingle()`, so duplicates never trigger a fresh insert again. It also handles a lost insert-race by fetching the winner.
2. **Cleaned up the 256 extras** (migration 00258) — collapsed to one Trip Cost per event, keeping the earliest. Crucially, it **repointed** any option whose `depends_on_option_id` pointed at a doomed Trip Cost to the survivor *before* deleting (the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so otherwise those options would silently lose their "requires attending" dependency).
3. **Guard against recurrence** — a partial unique index `idx_v2_options_one_trip_cost ON v2_options(event_id) WHERE option_type='trip_cost'`, so a second Trip Cost per event is now impossible at the DB level.

Done. Choice costs are now picked through a modal that shows **every** assignable cost.

## What changed

Each choice accordion's open body now has:
- The **label** input (immediate-save).
- The **applied costs** for that choice, shown as chips (name + amount).
- A **"Choose costs"** button → opens a modal.
- **Remove choice**.

**The cost picker modal** (`Costs for <choice>`):
- Lists **every assignable cost** — not just this option's and the unassigned pool, but costs currently used by *other* options too (`allAssignableItems` = all options' items + the available pool). Nothing is hidden for having been used before.
- **Categorized and sort-ordered** via the same `groupItems` grouping the Financials screen uses (contests first, then categories, each sorted by `sort_order`).
- Each row is a toggle with a checkmark showing whether it applies to this choice. Tap to toggle.

Because a cost can only live on one option (single `linked_option_id`), applying a cost that's currently on **another** option **moves it here** — I noted that in the modal's hint ("moving one here takes it off whatever option it was on before"). Within this option, a cost can still apply to several choices.

The choice header still shows that choice's own total, and the parent option header still shows the `$0–$74` range. tsc, eslint, and the build all pass.

## Verify
1. Open a choice → "Choose costs" → the modal lists all costs, grouped by contest/category, in sort order — including ones already applied to other choices/options.
2. Toggle a cost on/off; the choice's chips and header total update; close/reopen reflects it.
3. Apply a cost that was on a different option → it moves here (disappears from the other option, its price updates).
4. Apply the same cost to two different choices of this option → both show it; the member sees the right per-choice price.
5. Reorder choices by dragging; rename a choice (cost links survive); remove a choice (its costs detach cleanly).
The options building is excellent now!

Glad it landed well — that was a good iterative run. 🎉

For a quick recap of where the Options builder ended up:
- **Sections and the options list** are clean, de-boxed, full-width, with one unified drag system (reorder sections, move options between them, Trip Cost draggable like any option).
- **Choices** are draggable accordions showing each choice's own cost, with a categorized modal to assign any cost to a choice (costs can span choices, moving across options when needed).
- **The Trip Cost pileup** is fixed and guarded (one per event, enforced at the DB).

# v2: attendance-change integrity + immediate admin alerts (Lane A integrity)

Part of #214. Depends on #215. The hard one: a member who was "Attending" when teams/tee times were built later bails, and that quietly breaks a scramble team (empty seat), a tee time, or a Calcutta lot. An admin must **know immediately**.

This is the fix for v1's single biggest weakness here: v1 *computed* guarded-removal warnings and then threw them away — the admin grid (`AttendanceGrid.tsx`) silently discarded them. v2 has a real notification system, so we finish the job.

## What breaks when a participant leaves (v2 today: nothing guards it)
- `v2_scramble_team_members` — an orphaned/empty team seat (no FK cascade, no guard).
- `v2_scramble_hole_scores` — scores tied to a now-broken team.
- `v2_contest_winners` — if they'd already been recorded a winner.
- Tee times — v2 has only a `v2_scramble_teams.tee_time` field today (no pairing table yet); guard the seat, extend when real tee times land.
- Paid Options (#216) — leaving a paid contest must reverse the ledger charge.

## Behavior: never block — detect, remove, and inform

Hard rule (from the "can't be too sticky" principle in #215): **no attendance change or participation edit is ever refused**, even when it breaks downstream state. "Integrity" here means *detect and surface* breakage (and offer cleanup), not *prevent* it. This is a deliberate departure from v1, which refused guarded removals.

**Member drops their own RSVP** (likelihood < 99 via `/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`): honor reality — they're not coming. Cascade them off teams, Included contests, and opted-in Options (reversing those ledger charges). Then **alert admins** for every contest where it left a hole.

**Admin toggles someone off, or edits a single contest's participants** (the common partial case — left early, or a drop-in added to one round): apply the change as requested — **never blocked**. For any contest where it orphans protected state (empty scramble seat, a tee time, a recorded winner, a Calcutta bid when that lands), raise a **warning + admin alert + "needs attention"** flag so a human fixes the team, rather than silently leaving it broken.

The difference between the two paths is only *scope* (full roster leave vs a single-contest edit), not whether removal is allowed — it always is.

## The alert (the actual new capability)
- New notification type `contest_roster_break` in the v2 notification catalog (`notification-prefs.ts`).
- On a roster-affecting removal, send via `sendV2Notifications` to **all active org owners/admins** (query `v2_memberships` `role IN ('owner','admin')`, `status='active'`, `archived_at IS NULL`). In-app row **and** web push.
- Deep-link `data.url` to the affected contest's Teams page.
- Title/body name the member + what broke ("Dana Reyes left — Team 3 now has an empty seat in Round 1").

## "Needs attention" surfacing (in-app, beyond the push)
- Flag the affected team/contest as **needs attention** (derived: a team with fewer members than expected, or an enrolled seat whose member is no longer `on_roster`). Badge it on the contest list + Teams page so it's visible even if the push is missed.
- No new table needed if derivable; add a lightweight `needs_attention_at` only if derivation is too expensive.

## Edge cases
- Member re-RSVPs "Attending" after bailing: additive re-enroll (per #215), but do **not** silently reinstate a torn-down team seat — leave that to the admin (surface it as resolved/needs-review).
- Simulator-suppressed notifications inherited from `sendV2Notifications`.
- Best-effort alerts: a notification failure never blocks the attendance write.
- Don't double-alert on a no-op (member already off).

## Acceptance criteria
- Removing a member from a contest/team is **never blocked**, even with protected state — it applies, and an alert + "needs attention" flag is raised instead.
- A member dropping RSVP while on a team removes them and fires an admin push + in-app alert deep-linking to that team.
- Admin removing a member who's on a team gets a warning + alert and the affected team is flagged needs-attention (not silently left broken).
- Leaving a paid option reverses the member's ledger charge (coord. #216).
- The affected contest/team shows a "needs attention" badge until an admin resolves it.
- No alert on no-op removals.

#217 (attendance integrity) is built. Build, typecheck, and lint all pass. **One migration to run: `00259`** (adds `needs_attention_at` to `v2_scramble_teams`).

## What changed

**The leave cascade** (`cascadeLeaveRoster` in `enrollment.ts`) — the RSVP route's leave path was a stale stub ("v2 has no contest system yet"). Now, when a member drops below "Attending" or clears their RSVP, they're cascaded off everything they only had by attending:
- **Included contests** — removed, with *no* tombstone, so re-RSVPing "Attending" re-enrolls them additively.
- **Scramble team seats** — pulled, and the team flagged `needs_attention_at`.
- **Opted-in Options** — selections deleted (which reverses the derived charges) and option-driven contest enrollment reversed.

**The admin alert** (`alertRosterBreaks`) — a new `contest_roster_break` notification (added to the prefs catalog under "Admin alerts") fires to all active org owners/admins (in-app + push), deep-linked to the broken team's Teams page: *"Dana left, a team needs attention — Team 3 in Round 1 now has an empty seat."* Best-effort; never blocks the RSVP.

**"Needs attention" surfacing** — a badge on the admin **contests list** and a banner on the **Teams page**, both derived from `needs_attention_at`. They clear automatically when an admin re-saves teams (the Teams PUT replaces all rows).

**Bonus fix** — admin participant removal (`removeContestParticipants`) was leaving a dangling team seat; it now pulls the seat and flags the team too, so the badge covers that path.

## Verify (after running 00259)
1. On the TKO event, build a scramble team, then from another session drop that member's RSVP below "Attending" → they vanish from the team, the team shows an empty seat, the contests list shows a **Needs attention** badge, the Teams page shows the banner, and org admins get a push.
2. Clear an RSVP entirely → same cascade.
3. Re-RSVP "Attending" → re-enrolled into Included contests (no tombstone blocking), but the torn team seat stays flagged until an admin re-saves teams.
4. A member who'd selected paid Options bails → their selections clear and the derived balance drops.
5. Save the Teams screen → badge/banner clear.
6. No alert when a non-attending member re-confirms a lower likelihood (no-op).

## Still open in this epic
- **Member balances (#214)** — the "what you owe" screen (ledger table exists, unused).
- **Payouts / denominations.**
- Minor #217 tail: admin per-contest removals flag the team but don't yet *push* (badge still shows).

content.text:
Member balances is built, guided by v1 — and it needs **no migration** (the ledger table shipped back in 00253). Build, typecheck, and lint all pass.

## What I built

**The money model** (`src/lib/v2/balances.ts`) — mirrors v1's compute, adapted to v2's derived charges:
- `owed` = Trip Cost (if on-roster) + each selected Option's current price + any ledger charges
- `paid` = ledger payments
- `balance` = owed − paid (positive = owes)

Derived charges are computed live and never written to the ledger; the ledger (`v2_financial_transactions`) holds only payments, credits, and manual charges.

**Member — "My Balance"** (`/new/[slug]/balance`, in the Everything menu):
- A balance card: **"Balance due $X" / "You have a credit $X" / "All settled up"**, color-coded (v1's labels).
- **What you owe**: Trip Cost + each selected option (with its chosen choice as a sub-line), subtotaled as **Owed**.
- **Payments & credits**: each payment with method, subtotaled as **Paid**.
- Members only ever see their own money.

**Admin — "Balances"** (linked from the Financials header, `.../financials/balances`):
- A sortable **Member / Owed / Paid / Balance** grid with a **Totals** row (v1's FinancialGrid shape), scoped to the event (everyone on-roster plus any drop-in with a selection or charge).
- Tap a member → modal with their full breakdown (derived charges flagged "Derived", ledger payments removable) + a **Record** form: Payment / Credit / Winnings / Manual charge / Expense, with amount, method, description, notes. Writes recompute the balance live.

**APIs**: member `GET /balance`; admin `GET /balances/[userId]` (drill-in) and `POST`/`DELETE /transactions`.

## Verify (no migration needed)
1. As a member who's Attending with options picked → "My Balance" shows Trip Cost + options, Owed total, "Balance due".
2. Admin → Financials → Balances → the member shows matching Owed; tap them, record a $100 Venmo payment → Paid updates, balance drops, member's page reflects it.
3. Record a credit and a manual charge → both flow through; remove one → balance recomputes.
4. A non-attending drop-in given a manual charge appears in the grid.
5. Totals row sums correctly; a fully-paid member reads "All settled up".

## Known gaps vs v1 (deliberately deferred)
Transaction editing (delete+re-add works), audit history, Venmo deep link, search/date filters. Say the word and I'll add any of them.

Both things are fixed. tsc, eslint, and the build all pass.

## 1. RSVP speed + optimism

**Server** (`/api/v2/events/[eventId]/rsvp`) — the write now returns immediately; every side-effect (contest enrollment sync, the #217 leave cascade, admin push alerts, event-channel membership, activity logging) runs **after** the response via Next's `after()`. That's where the "incredibly slow" came from — all of that was blocking the response.

**Client** (`RsvpModule`) — changing your response is now **optimistic**: the UI updates instantly (status + the response/attending counts), the modal closes, and the request fires in the background; it reverts and reopens only if the save fails. No more waiting on the POST plus a second `loadParticipants` round-trip.

## 2. The model correction (you were right)

I read the v1 code and confirmed I'd diverged. v1: **Trip Cost is a normal selectable option** (price auto-derived from `included_in_trip_cost` items), and **options have zero ties to attendance**. I ripped out my invented "Trip Cost = attending" model:

- **Member options** (page, `OptionsModule`, home `OptionsReminder`/`HomeModules`): Trip Cost now renders as a regular selectable checkbox (price = the derived trip-cost total). No RSVP wiring, no "tap to join," no attendance gating. Dependencies are purely option-to-option.
- **Balances**: Trip Cost counts when the member **selects the Trip Cost option**, not when they're on the roster.
- **#217 leave cascade**: no longer clears option selections — options are independent of attendance. It still cascades off Included contests + scramble seats (those *do* tie to attendance in v1, correctly).
- **Admin builder**: new options no longer auto-depend on Trip Cost, and the "requires attending" label is gone — Trip Cost is just another option in the depends-on list.

I also recorded the correction in memory so I don't repeat it.

All green. Here's what was happening and the fix:

**Why nothing showed:** the "Choices" section (where you add the selectable choices + assign their per-choice costs) keys off the option's **saved** type, and it also required at least one existing choice. So when you switched the type to "Select one" in the editor (a draft change) with no choices yet, that section stayed hidden and the old "Bundled costs" area showed instead.

**Fix (two parts):**
1. **Changing the type now saves immediately** for an existing option — so the moment you pick "Select one," it persists and the Choices section appears right away (no manual save needed first). This matters because choices can only attach to an option whose saved type actually supports them.
2. **The Choices section now shows for any choice-type option**, even with zero choices — so you get the **"+ Add choice"** button (and the draggable choice accordions, each with its "Choose costs" picker) immediately.

All four requests are done — tsc, eslint, and the build pass (migration 260 applied).

## 1. "Your total" is now a floating bar
On the options page it's pinned above the bottom nav (and the music mini-player, using the same `--nav-h`/`--mini-h` offsets), always visible and updating live as you pick. The wizard summary keeps its own inline total.

## 2. Home wizard → plain link

## 3. "I'm not having any" is now configurable (not hardcoded)
To answer your question directly: it *was* hardcoded (auto-shown for required quantity with a fixed string). Now it's authored in the **option editor**:
- On a **Quantity** option, a toggle: **"Offer an 'I'm not having any' opt-out"** + an optional custom **label** (defaults to "I'm not having any").
- Stored on `v2_options.allow_none` / `none_label` (migration 00260).
- The member sees the opt-out only when you've enabled it, with your label. Picking it records a valid "none" answer ($0) that satisfies a required option.

## 4. (from before) Beer-style opt-out mechanics
The `{}` "answered-none" state works end-to-end: it satisfies required, costs $0, and — correctly — does **not** reveal options that *depend* on the quantity option (dependency needs a real quantity, matching v1).

## Verify
1. Options page: "Your total" floats at the bottom, updates as you toggle; the last option isn't hidden behind it.
2. Home: the "Complete your options" card links to the options page (pulses if required items are unanswered); no modal.
3. Admin → a Quantity option (e.g. Beer) → enable the opt-out, optionally rename it → Save. Member sees it; tapping it marks "none" and satisfies the required option at $0; tapping again clears it.
4. A non-quantity option shows no opt-out config.

Yes — the lock rule is installed and I just verified it end-to-end:

- **Server-enforced**: the pick API rejects any save once `isSlateLocked` is true (403 "Picks are locked"), so it can't be bypassed.
- **Whole slate, first start**: locks when `now ≥ the earliest game's start time` (exactly v1 — not per-game).

- **Simulator-aware**: uses `v2Now()`, so your admin time-sim works.

Here's the honest full-parity scorecard against v1's rules:

**Done (Phase 1):**
- ✅ Slate locks at first start time (server + UI)
- ✅ Scoring is **against the spread** (correct = covered)
- ✅ One **tiebreaker** game (guess total points); ties broken by closest
- ✅ Leaderboard: correct DESC → closest tiebreaker (a filled tiebreaker beats none)
- ✅ Individual picks **hidden until lock** (no early peeking)
- ✅ Open/closed admin toggle (members only see it when open)
- ✅ ✓/✗ once results are entered

**Not yet — Phase 2 (money):**
- ❌ Entry fee, pot, **%-of-pot payouts** ($5 rounding), payment tracking, Venmo button

Done — Phase 2 (money) + Reset are in, and crucially **reusing the existing money system** instead of a bespoke table. tsc, eslint, and the build pass. No new migration needed (I deleted the pickem-payments one before it was applied).

## How Pick'em money works now

- **Entry fee = the contest buy-in** (`setContestBuyIn`, a `buy_in_cost_item_id`), exactly like skins/CTP. In the Pick'em admin there's now an **Entry fee** field.
- **Members pay by opting into it as an Option** — you bundle the Pick'em contest into an Option (the normal Options builder), members select it, get charged in their **Balance**, and auto-enrolled. That's the whole "it's an option like everything else" flow — no separate payments table.
- **Payout splits** — an editable "% of pot" list (1st/2nd/3rd…), stored in the contest's `payout_splits`.
- **Pot + payouts display** — `Pot: $fee × N in = $pot`, split into whole-$5 amounts per place (v1's rounding, ported to cents). This tells you how much to pay each place.
- **Paying winners** — record a **winnings** entry on the **Balances** screen (the ledger), so it's the same money system everywhere.
- **Reset** — a destructive "Reset picks" button (with confirm) clears everyone's picks; the game slate + results stay.

One deliberate deviation from v1 I noted in memory: the leaderboard isn't gated to "paid" anymore — payment lives in the ledger now, so the board shows anyone who picked.

## Verify
1. Admin → Pick'em → set an **Entry fee**, add **payout splits** (e.g. 50/30/20) → the Pot/payouts line updates as members enroll.
2. Create an **Option** that bundles the Pick'em contest → a member selects it → their **Balance** shows the charge; they're enrolled (pot count goes up).
3. Enter results → leaderboard ranks → pay the winner a **winnings** entry on **Balances**.
4. **Reset picks** → confirm → all picks cleared, games/results intact.

**Participant management for Pick'em — done.** The admin screen now has a **Players** card (shows "N enrolled") linking to the standard enroll/remove page — the same In / Not-in checklist every contest uses, so you can add on-site opt-ins or remove people. - A **shared payout-splits editor** on every contest's settings (not just Pick'em).

- Per-type **winner determination** feeding it (skins + Pick'em have it; scramble/CTP/LD/etc. would each need their winner logic wired in).

Done — the payout module now matches v1's options. tsc, lint, and build all pass.

## What the payout editor supports now (v1 parity)
Each place's cut can be set to one of v1's kinds:
- **% of pot** — percentage of the pot.
- **$ amount** — a flat dollar figure (e.g., 2nd = **$80**).
- **Remainder** — whatever's left after the fixed/% places (your "winner gets the rest").
- **Winner takes all** — the whole pot to one place.

The math (`computePlacePayouts`, ported from v1's `payout-events/splits.ts`) applies them in priority: a single-winner short-circuits; flat + percentage take their cut; **remainder absorbs the rest** (first remainder honored). Your exact example works — set **2nd = flat $80** and **1st = Remainder**, and 1st shows pot − $80.

This lives in the shared editor, so it's available on **every contest's** Payouts card (and Pick'em), and the team-aware split still applies on top (a team place divides evenly among members).

One deliberate change in matching v1: I dropped the Pick'em-only "round to $5" step — v1's general payout model pays exact amounts (remainder makes the pot total exactly). Say the word if you want $5-bill rounding back as an option.

## Verify
1. Any contest → **Payouts** → add two places: 1st = **Remainder**, 2nd = **$ amount** 80 → with a pot, 2nd shows $80 and 1st shows the rest.
2. Switch a place to **% of pot** → it takes that %; remainder recalculates.
3. **Winner takes all** → one place shows the full pot.
4. Team contest → the per-place amount still shows "→ $X each (team of N)".

input.content:
# Let team members rename their own team (v2)

## Overview

In the v2 admin flow, an admin can already rename a scramble team off the default
"Team N" via the Teams manager (`.../admin/events/{eventId}/contests/{contestId}/teams`).
We want the **members of a team** to be able to rename it too, from the member-facing
side of the app (not just admins).

This is a small, fun bit of ownership: a foursome names themselves ("The Shank Brothers"),
and that name shows wherever the team appears (scoreboards, tee sheets, standings).

## UX flow

- A member who is on a scramble team sees their team's name with an inline edit affordance
  (pencil / tap-to-edit) on whatever member screen surfaces their team (scoring / schedule /
  contest detail — TBD which surface(s)).
- Editing commits the new name; empty reverts to the "Team N" default placeholder.
- Name change is visible to teammates and admins in near-real-time (or on next load).
- Reasonable length cap (match the admin input: 40 chars) and trimming.

## Technical plan

- Team name lives on `v2_scramble_teams.name` (already editable by admins via the teams PUT).
- Add a member-scoped endpoint (e.g. `PATCH /api/v2/events/{eventId}/contests/{contestId}/teams/{teamId}/name`)
  that gates on "requester is a member of that team" (via `v2_scramble_team_members`) OR an admin.
  Use `getEffectiveUserId` + the admin client so RLS doesn't silently no-op.
- Keep the admin teams PUT as-is; this is an additive, narrowly-scoped write (name only).
- Decide the member surface(s) to mount the editor on.

## Edge cases

- Member removed from the team after starting an edit → reject (not on team anymore).
- Two teammates editing at once → last write wins (fine for a name).
- Name collides with another team's name → allow (names aren't unique).
- Guests / non-members viewing → read-only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A team member can rename their own team from a member-facing screen.
- [ ] A non-member (and non-admin) cannot rename a team they're not on.
- [ ] Admins can still rename any team from the Teams manager.
- [ ] Cleared name falls back to the "Team N" default everywhere.
- [ ] New name propagates to all surfaces that display the team.

## Notes

Filed per user request while building the admin teams drag-to-reorder + payouts-modal work.
Deferred to an issue intentionally (not built yet).

---
name: feedback_autosave_everywhere
description: Never require a Save button; every change should auto-save (debounced background write) with a subtle status note
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

The user wants to **never click "Save" anywhere in the app**. Every editable surface should persist changes automatically. The app had gotten inconsistent (some auto-save, some gated behind a Save button) and the user wants it uniformly auto-save.

**Why:** Save buttons are friction and easy to forget; auto-save is the expected modern behavior.

**How to apply:** Debounce a background write (~700ms) on any change; mirror state in a ref so the debounced closure reads the latest value; only flip to "saved" if nothing changed while the request was in flight (`ref.current === snapshot`). Done. Now your two questions:

## 1. 3-man teams → A/B/C?

Yes, exactly. The generator divides the field into **as many skill classes as the team size**:
- **4-man** → A/B/C/D (4 tiers), each team gets one random player from each.
- **3-man** → A/B/C (3 tiers).
- **2-man** → A/B.

Mechanically: `numTeams = ceil(field ÷ teamSize)`, then the field is sliced into `ceil(field ÷ numTeams)` tiers (which works out to the team size), A = lowest handicaps down to the last tier. Each tier is shuffled, then dealt one per team. So with 12 players at 3-man you get 4 teams, each with one random A, one random B, one random C.

## 2. Do the three bottom-pinned things play nicely?

They do **now** — but your instinct was right, they didn't before I fixed it. Here's the layering:

- **Bottom nav** — reserved via `--nav-h`, sits at the very bottom, `z-[60]`.
- **Music mini-player** — reserved via `--mini-h`, floats directly *above* the nav.
- **Save chip** — must clear *both*.

content.text:
I dug in and verified the specifics. Here's what I found — de-noised to genuine "forced capability that should be an admin option," with the audit's false positives discarded.

## Your example, confirmed (and it's worse than it looks)

The scramble scorer's **Green** (`on_green`) and **Putt** (`holed_out`) toggles are hardcoded into both the admin scorer (`ScoringManager.tsx:281-282`) and written to `v2_contest_observations` on every hole. But I traced the consumers: **nothing reads them back except the scorecard review itself.** No contest (100 Feet, BSPITW, etc.) actually computes off them yet. So right now they're forced data-collection with no payoff — exactly the kind of thing that should be opt-in per scramble.

The clean fix: store `track_greens` / `track_putts` (or a `observations: [...]` list) in the scramble's `config` JSONB (which already exists on `v2_contests`), set at scramble creation/settings, and have both scorers hide the toggles when off.

## Other genuine leaks (verified)

1. **Contest `auto_enroll` and `scoring_source` are forced by type.** `defaultAutoEnroll()`/`defaultScoringSource()` in `contests.ts` hardcode behavior per contest type. The DB columns are per-contest configurable, but **no creation UI exposes them** — so an admin can't make a scramble opt-in, or flip a contest between auto-scored and hand-adjudicated.

2. **Managed chat channels are always created.** `ensureAllMembersRoom()` / `ensureEventRoom()` auto-create with no opt-out — a group that doesn't want an all-members channel can't decline it.

3. **Event-span calendar banner always renders** for every active event (`schedule-feed.ts`) — no toggle.

4. **Side-game catalog is a fixed list of 4** (skins/CTP/LD/LP in `SideGames.tsx`) — not extensible per group. (Lower priority — it's a real list, just closed.)

## Discarded as non-issues (so you know I looked)

- **Individual-round stats** (putts/fairways/GIR/penalties) are **already configurable** — per *user* via `tracked_stats`. Arguably you'd want admins to be able to standardize/restrict them, but it's not "forced."
- Max strokes (20), max putts (10), tee-color hex map, min score (1), status enum — these are sensible constants, not capabilities anyone would toggle. The audit over-flagged them.

The underlying pattern is sound (feature registry + per-org columns + contest `config` JSONB); the problem is **incomplete wiring** — capabilities exist in schema but aren't surfaced as admin toggles.

# v2: close "forced capability" leaks (make admin-configurable)

## Principle

The v2 platform is meant to be fully customizable per group-admin: capabilities should be **opt-in options an admin configures**, not always-on defaults. A few capabilities leaked in as forced defaults. This issue tracks closing them so none are silently dropped.

The infrastructure already exists — the fix is almost always **wiring an existing config surface to an admin toggle**, not new plumbing:
- Feature registry: `src/lib/v2/features.ts` (+ `v2_event_features` per-org/per-event rows)
- Per-org columns: `v2_organizations` (e.g. `member_noun`, `show_birthdays`, `store_enabled`, `name_display`)
- Per-contest config: `v2_contests.config` JSONB

## DONE (2026-10-02)

- [x] **Scramble scorer forced greens/putts.** The scramble scorer always showed per-player "Green" (`on_green`) + "Putt" (`holed_out`) toggles and wrote `v2_contest_observations` on every hole — and nothing even consumed them downstream yet. Now gated by `config.track_greens` / `config.track_putts`, **off by default**, set in Contest settings (scramble only). Scorer hides the toggles when off. Files: `ContestSettings.tsx`, `ScoringManager.tsx`, `scoring/page.tsx`, contest detail `page.tsx`.

## TODO (verified leaks)

- [ ] **Contest `auto_enroll` / `scoring_source` forced by type.** `defaultAutoEnroll()` / `defaultScoringSource()` in `src/lib/v2/contests.ts` hardcode behavior per type. The DB columns are per-contest configurable, but no creation/settings UI exposes them — admins can't make a scramble opt-in, or flip a contest between auto-scored and hand-adjudicated. Fix: surface both as toggles in the contest create/settings flow.
- [ ] **Managed chat channels always created, no opt-out.** `ensureAllMembersRoom()` / `ensureEventRoom()` (`src/lib/v2/chat/channels.ts`) auto-create with no way to decline. Fix: per-org (and/or per-event) toggle; skip creation when off.
- [ ] **Event-span calendar banner always rendered.** Every active event auto-adds an all-day banner entry in `src/lib/v2/schedule-feed.ts`. Fix: per-event (or per-org) toggle.
- [ ] **Side-game catalog is a closed list of 4** (skins/CTP/LD/LP in `SideGames.tsx`). Lower priority — it's a real list, just not extensible per group.

## Explicitly NOT doing (considered, rejected as non-issues)

- Individual-round stats (putts/fairways/GIR/penalties) are already configurable per-user via `v2_profiles.tracked_stats`. (Possible future: let admins standardize/restrict the set per group — but not a "forced" bug.)
- Hardcoded constants that aren't capabilities anyone toggles: max strokes (20), max putts/penalties (10), tee-color hex map, min score (1), contest status enum.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Each TODO capability is either admin-configurable or consciously documented as always-on.
- [ ] Defaults for newly-exposed toggles preserve sensible behavior (opt-in where the capability is niche).

content.text:
You're right on both counts, and the schema actually agrees with you. Let me lay out what I found and what I'd recommend.

## Your instincts are both correct — and the original design backs them

**1. These aren't scramble data — they belong to the consuming contest.** Migration `00246` literally documents this:

> `v2_contest_observations is one generalized per-player store (on_green, holed_out, distance_in) that BSPITW / 100 Feet! / CTP all read from.`

So the observations table was always meant to be keyed to the *consuming* contest, read by BSPITW/CTP/100 Feet. My putting `track_greens`/`track_putts` on the **scramble** config was the wrong layer — I bolted the config onto the thing doing the data entry instead of the thing that needs the data. The scramble is just the scoring surface; it should collect whatever the live contests need.

**2. A super-admin catalog is both wanted and feasible.** `v2_profiles.is_system_admin` already exists (`isSystemAdmin()`, surfaced in context, with a system-admin landing on `/new`). And today the metric list is a hardcoded enum: `CHECK (metric IN ('on_green','holed_out','distance_in'))`. That's exactly the thing that should become a super-admin-managed catalog with real descriptions.

## The model I'd propose

- **`v2_scoring_metrics`** — super-admin catalog. `key`, `label`, `description` (the "so group admins understand" text), `value_type` (flag / distance / count), `sort_order`, `is_active`. Seeded with the current three. Replaces the hardcoded `CHECK` enum. System-admin CRUD UI in the existing system-admin area.
- **The consuming contest** (BSPITW, CTP, 100 Feet) is where a **group admin picks which metrics it collects**, choosing from the catalog and reading your descriptions. Stored in that contest's `config.metrics`.
- **The scramble scorer** collects the **union** of metrics required by the contests drawing from that round — child contests (`parent_contest_id` = this scramble, e.g. CTP) plus event-wide aggregates running that day (BSPITW, 100 Feet). Each toggle shows the catalog `label`; the description lives in the admin config.

## The one real open decision

Observations today are keyed `UNIQUE(contest_id, user_id, hole_number, metric)` — i.e. **per consuming contest**. But "Jeff was on the green on hole 5" is a physical fact two contests might both want. So either: (a) keep per-contest keying and let the scorer write one row per consuming contest that needs it, or (b) re-key observations to the **round** and have contests read shared facts. I lean (a) for now (matches the existing schema, no migration churn; duplication is cheap), and revisit if it gets messy.

## What I'd do about the code I just wrote

Revert the scramble-settings `track_greens`/`track_putts` toggles — they're in the wrong place. The catalog + consuming-contest selection replaces them.

-- 00262 v2 scoring metrics catalog (#220)
-- A super-admin (system-admin) curated catalog of per-player scoring observations
-- that a scramble scorer can collect (greens hit, holed out, distance to pin, ...).
-- Group admins pick which metrics a CONSUMING contest (BSPITW / 100 Feet / CTP)
-- collects; the scramble scorer then surfaces the union. Each metric carries a
-- description so group admins understand what it means.
--
-- Also relaxes the hardcoded metric CHECK on v2_contest_observations so new catalog
-- keys are storable (validation moves to the app, against this catalog).

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS public.v2_scoring_metrics CASCADE;

CREATE TABLE public.v2_scoring_metrics (
  id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  key         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,          -- stable slug stored in v2_contest_observations.metric
  label       TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- display name on the scorer toggle
  description TEXT,                           -- explanation shown to group admins
  value_type  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'flag'   -- 'flag' (0/1), 'distance' (inches), 'count'
              CHECK (value_type IN ('flag', 'distance', 'count')),
  sort_order  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  is_active   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE INDEX idx_v2_scoring_metrics_active ON public.v2_scoring_metrics(is_active, sort_order);

-- Seed the three metrics the observations store originally hardcoded.
INSERT INTO public.v2_scoring_metrics (key, label, description, value_type, sort_order) VALUES
  ('on_green',    'Greens hit',    'The player''s shot finished on the green for this hole.',        'flag',     0),
  ('holed_out',   'Holed out',     'The player sank the putt (made the shot) on this hole.',          'flag',     1),
  ('distance_in', 'Distance to pin','Measured distance of the player''s shot from the hole, in inches.','distance', 2)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

-- Relax the observations metric constraint: the catalog is now the source of truth.
ALTER TABLE public.v2_contest_observations DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS v2_contest_observations_metric_check;

ALTER TABLE public.v2_scoring_metrics ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY "v2_scoring_metrics_read" ON public.v2_scoring_metrics FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true);

GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.v2_scoring_metrics TO authenticated;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLE public.v2_scoring_metrics TO service_role;

Both your instincts were right, and I rebuilt it accordingly. Build is green.

## What I did

**Reverted the misplaced scramble toggles.** Removed `track_greens`/`track_putts` from the scramble's Contest settings. The scramble scorer no longer forces greens/putts — it collects nothing until a consuming contest asks for it. (I left the `trackGreens`/`trackPutts` gating in `ScoringManager`, fed `false` for now, so wiring it to consuming contests later is a one-line change — there's a `TODO(#220)` marker in `scoring/page.tsx`.)

**Built the super-admin scoring-metrics catalog** (the thing you asked for):
- `v2_scoring_metrics` (migration **00262**): `key`, `label`, **`description`**, `value_type` (yes-no / distance / count), `sort_order`, `is_active`. Seeded with greens hit / holed out / distance to pin. Also dropped the old hardcoded `metric` CHECK on `v2_contest_observations` so new catalog keys are storable.
- System-admin CRUD API at `/api/v2/admin/scoring-metrics` (gated by `isSystemAdmin`), and a management UI at **`/new/admin/scoring-metrics`** linked from Platform → Data management. You can add any number of metrics, each with a clear description for group admins. Delete is refused if a metric's already been collected (deactivate instead).
- I mirrored the existing **cost-categories** pattern exactly, so it's consistent with how the platform already manages shared catalogs.

**The model going forward** (per your "configure these on BSPITW" call): when BSPITW / 100 Feet / CTP get built, each consuming contest will declare which catalog metrics it collects (`config.metrics`), and the scramble scorer will surface the union of what the live contests need. The catalog is the groundwork; the per-contest selection + scorer-union is wired then. This is all captured in issue #220.

Since this adds a migration, you'll need to apply **00262** before the catalog page works.

### Verify
1. As a system admin, go to `/new/admin` → **Data management** → **Scoring metrics**. You see the 3 seeded metrics with descriptions and type badges.
2. Add a metric with a description → appears in the list; edit it → persists; deactivate/reactivate works.
3. Try to delete a seeded metric that's been used → refused with "deactivate instead"; an unused one deletes.
4. A non-system-admin hitting `/new/admin/scoring-metrics` → bounced to `/new`.
5. Open a scramble → Scoring: the per-player Green/Putt toggles are gone (collects nothing for now).
6. Contest settings for a scramble: no "Scoring options" section anymore.

One heads-up: existing scrambles that were collecting greens/putts will stop until the consuming-contest wiring lands — that's the intended interim, since nothing consumed that data anyway.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding Venmo API and developer programmatic payments:

## Current Status (2026)

As of July 24, 2026, Venmo has no official CLI, no official MCP server, and no consumer API open to new developers.

## Legacy Developer and Payouts APIs

Venmo's Developer and Payouts APIs have been retired, and they are no longer able to provide access to businesses who may want to start using it. However, retained access is generally limited to integrations grandfathered before 2016.

## Available Integration Options

For businesses looking to accept Venmo payments, Venmo's API is a powerful tool to help you seamlessly integrate payments into your application with the use of payment links, drop ins, OAuth, or the REST API. Integration options include Pay with Venmo checkout through Braintree or PayPal, and approval-gated PayPal Standard Payouts with recipient claim in Venmo.

## P2P and Consumer API Limitations

Agent-driven P2P sends, balance reads, and business-profile management have no official path: the retired consumer API is closed to new developers, and the User Agreement's restricted-activities language puts unofficial wrappers and credential sharing on the account holder's risk.

In summary, while Venmo does offer payment integration options for merchants, programmatic P2P payments and general developer API access for new developers are not available in 2026.

I researched the Venmo/PayPal reality, and it reshapes the plan significantly. Two hard constraints you need to know up front:

**1. There's no API to silently pull money from people.** Venmo's consumer/P2P API has been closed to new developers since ~2016 and is effectively retired. The only sanctioned paths today are merchant pay-ins via Braintree/PayPal ("Pay with Venmo" checkout) and **approval-gated** PayPal Standard Payouts (the recipient claims the money in Venmo). Agent-driven P2P sends and balance reads have no official path. So "automatically pull from the losers" isn't possible — every charge requires the payer to actively approve, and there's no way to debit someone on your schedule.

**2. Wagering is explicitly prohibited by both AUPs.** Venmo and PayPal both ban "any activity with an entry fee and a prize" (sports betting, pools, etc.) for non-approved accounts — which is exactly what a buy-in-then-winner-takes-pot side game is. The app itself collecting buy-ins and distributing winnings would make us an unapproved gambling operator under their terms, independent of the technical problem.

So the vision as literally described (app auto-collects from losers, auto-sends to winners) is blocked both technically and by policy.

**The feasible version is "settle-up links" (Splitwise-style).** We already track who-owes-whom in the balances/ledger (#214). On top of that, the app computes the net settlement and hands each person a **one-tap, prefilled Venmo payment link** to pay the person they owe. Money moves **peer-to-peer directly between friends** — the app never holds funds, never acts as a merchant, needs no KYC/licensing, and stays clear of the gambling-operator problem (it's friends settling a golf outing, not an app running a book). Your "approval step" becomes inherent: nothing moves until the payer taps and confirms in Venmo. The heavier custodial/merchant path is technically possible but realistically a non-starter for a friends' golf app (gambling-merchant approval + money-transmitter licensing + KYC + holding funds).

# Venmo/PayPal settle-up for side games & wagering

## Goal

Make settling side-game wagers frictionless: the app knows who owes whom (it already tracks the money), and hands each person a **one-tap, prefilled Venmo or PayPal payment link** so they can pay directly. Money moves peer-to-peer between people; **the app never holds or moves funds**.

## Feasibility research (why this shape, not "auto-pull and distribute")

The original vision — app automatically pulls from losers and sends to winners — is blocked on two independent fronts:

1. **No programmatic P2P API.** Venmo's consumer/P2P API has been closed to new developers since ~2016 and is effectively retired. The only sanctioned integrations are merchant pay-ins via Braintree/PayPal ("Pay with Venmo" checkout) and **approval-gated** PayPal Standard Payouts (recipient claims in Venmo). There is no way to silently debit a user or read balances. Every charge requires the payer to actively approve. (venmo.com/docs, fintechfutures)
2. **Wagering is prohibited by both AUPs.** Venmo and PayPal both ban transactions for "any activity with an entry fee and a prize" (pools, betting, etc.) for non-approved accounts. The app collecting buy-ins and distributing winnings would make us an unapproved gambling operator under their terms. (PayPal Acceptable Use Policy; Venmo User Agreement)

**Decision:** build the **settle-up links** model (Splitwise-style). The app is an information/convenience layer only. This needs no PayPal merchant account, no KYC, no money-transmitter licensing, no custody — and keeps us clear of the gambling-operator problem because friends are settling a shared golf outing directly, not transacting with an app that runs a book.

**Compliance posture (keep to these):** never hold funds; never act as payee/intermediary; only generate links and record who-said-they-paid. Frame copy around settling a shared activity, not "gambling debts."

## Two contexts, two topologies (confirmed with product)

| | One-off personal round | Event contest |
|---|---|---|
| Source of truth | `v2_round_games` (skins/nassau/etc.) | `v2_financial_transactions` ledger (#214) |
| Topology | **Mesh** — peer-to-peer among players | **Hub-and-spoke** — each member nets to one balance vs. the event treasurer |
| Settlement math | Net all games, then minimize transactions (greedy debtor/creditor) | Each member already has ONE net number; settle member ↔ treasurer |
| Trigger | After the round completes; player-driven | Admin-released by the event organizer |
| Approval step | Opt-in when a money game includes you | Enrollment already is the opt-in; admin controls release |

## Data model

- **Payment handles on `v2_profiles`** (new migration): `venmo_handle TEXT`, `paypal_handle TEXT`, optional `payout_pref TEXT` (venmo|paypal). Set in account settings. Nullable; settle-up degrades gracefully when missing (show "ask them for their handle").
- **Event treasurer/payee** (hub model): which member + handle collects/disburses the event pot. Likely `v2_events` column or event settings (`treasurer_user_id`). The organizer by default.
- **Settlement records:**
  - Event: reuse `v2_financial_transactions` — a `payment` row with `method='venmo'|'paypal'` records a member settling; the schema already supports this (`type`, `source`, `method`). Add a lightweight "settlement intent/confirmed" state if we want a requested→paid→confirmed lifecycle.
  - Personal round: add a small `v2_round_game_settlements` (or a `settled_at`/`settled_method` on a per-pair row) since round games have no ledger. TBD in design.

## Link generation

- **Venmo deep link:** `https://venmo.com/?txn=pay&audience=private&recipients=<handle>&amount=<amt>&note=<note>` (opens app on mobile, web fallback). Validate/normalize handles.
- **PayPal:** `https://paypal.me/<handle>/<amount>`.
- Prefill amount + a note ("Golfapalooza skins, 6/14"). Note: links can't be forced private/verified — see trust gap below.

## Settlement computation

- **Mesh (personal):** sum every game into a net per player, then greedy min-cash-flow (largest creditor ↔ largest debtor) to minimize the number of payments. Netted across the whole round per the product decision.
- **Hub (event):** the ledger already nets each member to a single balance; net-negative members pay the treasurer, treasurer pays net-positive members. No cross-member links.

## UX flows

1. **Account setup** — add Venmo/PayPal handle(s) in profile/account. One-time.
2. **Inclusion/approval** — when a money game includes you (personal round), confirm you're in the money pool (your requested approval step). Event enrollment already serves as opt-in.
3. **Settle-up screen** —
   - "You owe **@winner $12** → [Pay with Venmo] [Pay with PayPal]" (one tap, prefilled).
   - "You're owed **$8 from Dave**" → [Send a reminder] (Venmo request link / nudge notification).
   - **Mark as paid** / **Mark as received** (manual, both sides can confirm — see trust gap).
4. **Notifications** — personal: fire on round completion to each player. Event: fire when the admin releases settle-up.

## Trust gap (important)

Because there's no Venmo API, the app **cannot verify a payment actually happened**. Settlement is self-reported: payer taps "I paid," payee confirms "received." Model a `requested → paid → confirmed` lifecycle and surface unconfirmed items. This is the same limitation Splitwise has; acceptable for a friends' app.

## Phasing

- **P1:** profile payment handles + personal-round mesh settle-up (net-minimized) + one-tap Venmo/PayPal links + mark-paid/confirm.
- **P2:** event hub settle-up (admin release, treasurer config, ledger `payment` rows, member↔treasurer links).
- **P3:** request-money nudges, reminders, settle-up status dashboard, reconciliation polish.

## Explicitly out of scope

- App custody of funds, auto-debit, escrow, holding a pot.
- Acting as a payment facilitator / gambling merchant.
- Guaranteed/verified payment confirmation (no API exists).

## Open questions

- Event treasurer: always the organizer, or configurable per event? What if the pot is split across multiple payees (v1 had cash denominations per payout sheet)?
- Personal-round settlements storage: new table vs. columns on an existing one.
- Minimum-viable handle validation (Venmo usernames change; no lookup API).
- Do we want PayPal "request money" links for the owed side, or just reminders?
- International/other rails (Cash App, Zelle) — deferred; Venmo+PayPal first.
